 Develop and maintain reporting frameworks and dashboards to support data-driven decision-making, identify performance trends, and guide budget allocation.
- 
 Lead the creative briefing process by identifying effective hooks, messaging angles, formats, and concepts based on campaign performance and audience insights.
- 
 Collaborate with content, creative, and product teams to develop high-converting advertising assets and landing pages, continuously improving the customer journey.
- 
 Implement creative testing systems and processes to reduce creative fatigue, increase production velocity, and maintain campaign effectiveness at scale.
- 
 Build and maintain strong relationships with advertising platforms, traffic sources, and external partners, negotiating premium placements and customized commercial opportunities.
- 
 Research and test new acquisition channels, advertising networks, formats, and tools, establishing clear evaluation criteria before scaling successful initiatives.
- 
 Stay informed about advertising ecosystem developments, platform policies, algorithm changes, and market trends, adapting strategies to maintain performance and compliance.
- 
 Identify opportunities to automate campaign management, reporting, and acquisition workflows through internal tools and technology.

 Create standard operating procedures, playbooks, and structured experimentation pipelines to improve operational efficiency and support sustainable growth.

 Contribute to ambitious user acquisition objectives, including scaling existing campaigns to more than three times their current budgets and supporting significant expansion of the global user base.

 Between 4 and 10+ years of professional experience in performance marketing, paid acquisition, or user acquisition, with a strong track record of delivering measurable growth.

- 
 Proven ability to take full ownership of campaign strategy, execution, budget management, optimization, and performance results.

 Hands-on experience with major paid acquisition platforms, including Meta, TikTok, Snapchat, Apple Search Ads, Google, or native advertising networks.

 Strong analytical capabilities and practical experience with GA4, Voluum, conversion tracking, attribution setups, reporting dashboards, and performance measurement tools.

 Strong creative instincts and experience developing advertising briefs, identifying effective hooks and messaging angles, analyzing creative performance, and iterating quickly.

 Highly goal-oriented, proactive, and accountable, with a strong sense of ownership and commitment to measurable business outcomes.
-

- 
 Strong attention to detail and a continuous improvement mentality, with a focus on speed, performance, and rapid iteration.
- 
 Humility, openness to feedback, and willingness to learn, experiment, and collaborate with colleagues.
- 
 Comfort working with products that may include uncensored AI-generated models and NSFW (not safe for work) content, including advertising within this category.

 At least 6 years of relevant professional experience.

 Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications and collaboration tools, including Microsoft Teams and SharePoint.

title: Business Operations Associate
description:
About Us
 Fanatics is building a leading global digital sports platform. We ignite the passions of global sports fans and maximize the presence and reach for our hundreds of sports partners globally by offering products and services across Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, and Fanatics Betting & Gaming, allowing sports fans to Buy, Collect, and Bet. Through the Fanatics platform, sports fans can buy licensed fan gear, jerseys, lifestyle and streetwear products, headwear, and hardgoods; collect physical and digital trading cards, sports memorabilia, and other digital assets; and bet as the company builds its Sportsbook and iGaming platform. Fanatics has an established database of over 100 million global sports fans; a global partner network with approximately 900 sports properties, including major national and international professional sports leagues, players associations, teams, colleges, college conferences and retail partners, 2,500 athletes and celebrities, and 200 exclusive athletes; and over 2,000 retail locations, including its Lids retail stores. Our more than 22,000 employees are committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience and delighting sports fans globally. 
 Overview 
 Fanatics is looking for a Business Operations Associate to run the systems behind Fanatics ONE benefits and to make sure every dollar the program spends gets charged to the right budget.
 Fanatics ONE is the loyalty program that recognizes fans across the Fanatics ecosystem. Members earn gifts and access to events they can't buy anywhere else, from seats at sold-out games to Fanatics Fest.
 Every gift campaign and member event has a back office behind it. Someone has to price the tickets, code the expenses, track the invoices and bill other teams when they use what we've paid for. That work keeps growing as more of the company shares our tickets and events. Right now, that responsibility is spread across several people within their own functions, so this role brings it together in one place, with a view across the whole program.
 A big part of the job is TicketManager, the system where we hold tickets and suites for sports and concerts. Colleagues across Fanatics claim seats from it. We want to open more of that inventory to other teams so we can pool budgets and buy more, and that only works if every seat carries a real price and every claim gets billed to the team that used it.
 This is a systems role first and a finance role second. The person who does well here likes building and fixing the tools a team runs on, and has an eye to catch financial numbers that don’t add up.
 You'll report to the Senior Manager, Strategy & Partnerships and work closely with Gifting Operations, Event Production, Bespoke Benefits, Finance, and our analytics team.
 Responsibilities 
 TicketManager and ticket inventory
- Own pricing for our tickets and suites, and keep it current as the market changes
- Apply the team's pricing approach and flag any price that looks off
- Make sure the right team or business pays for the seats it uses
- Work with Event Production so our ticket records match what happened at each event
- Report on how our tickets get used, including seats that go unclaimed
- Manage day-to-day operations of Fanatics Fest ticketing
 Intake and systems
- Run our request intake day to day, so every request gets to the right team with a cost and a timeline
- Keep our records and budget codes clean so reports don't need fixing by hand
- Build automations and small tools that replace manual tracking
- Show teammates how to submit requests and expenses the right way
 Spend and cross-charges
- Review and reconcile spending across teams, and help fix anything coded incorrectly
- Handle cross-charges when other Fanatics teams and businesses use our inventory
- Help set up vendors and keep invoices moving until they're paid
- Keep budget coding accurate as people and programs shift between teams
 Month-end and reporting
- Prepare the monthly reconciliation with Finance so our numbers match theirs
- Track spend against budget, and answer questions about where a charge came from and who should cover it
 Who you are 
- Details matter to you. When you spot a miscoded expense or a mispriced seat, you fix it right away.
- You can look at a complicated process that runs across several teams and systems and work out how the pieces fit together.
- Building things is how you solve problems. If a task gets done by hand every week, you want to automate it, and you enjoy making the work easier for everyone around you.
- You work well with people on other teams, and you know how to ask a busy colleague for help in a way that's easy to say yes to.
- When something is waiting on someone else, you follow up until it's done.

- 1 to 2 years of experience in operations, finance, ticketing or a related field
- Has worked hands-on in a database or workflow tool such as Airtable
- Comfortable using AI tools in your everyday work
- Strong spreadsheet skills in Excel or Google Sheets

OUR PRODUCT CHALLENGE 

The bottleneck isn't demand, it's supply. There aren't enough experts to serve every family who needs us. To scale to all of America, we have to unbundle expertise from the human so that anyone who can foster human connection can become a Hero. 

The problem is that this expertise is tribal knowledge. One social worker knows how to expedite Medicaid in New York, another knows which home-visiting PT families actually love. It's trapped in people's heads.  

To solve this,  our platform captures every interaction and turns it into compounding intelligence that makes every user smarter. Think Waymo: expert humans do the driving today, and every mile they log trains the system so that tomorrow, anyone — even with zero healthcare background — can perform like a 20-year veteran. The hard part is building a system that knows what to trust, what's gone stale, what's local versus universal, and how to surface the right insight at the right moment. $150,000-$200,000 base salary + meaningful early equity · Full-time

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are hiring our first finance hire to build the finance function of Revin from the ground up. You will work directly with our VP of Operations and leadership to own the numbers that run the company: the model, the forecast, and every dollar that moves in or out.



This is a founding, hands-on role. You will build the model and also close the books. You will set the forecast and also chase the invoice. There is no team beneath you on day one, you are the team, and you will design the systems and hire against them as we scale.



The honest pitch: we are handing you the financial operating system of a company that is about to get much bigger, much faster. If you want to own finance end-to-end at a company on a steep curve, and turn a spreadsheet into the infrastructure a board runs on, this is the seat.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Own the financial model. Build and maintain the model that leadership and the board run the business on. Own the forecast, defend every assumption, and keep the model honest as reality moves.

 - Run the close. Own month-end close end-to-end: accruals, reconciliations, and clean, on-time financials leadership can trust. Design the close process so it gets faster every month, not slower.

 - Own billing and AR. Own the full order-to-cash cycle: invoicing, collections, and revenue integrity. Every dollar that should come in, comes in, on time, and ties out.

 - Drive planning and capital strategy. Own burn, runway, and scenario planning. Build the dashboards and board materials that turn raw numbers into decisions, and partner on fundraising when the time comes.

 - Run ROI and unit economics. Be the analytical partner to the business: pricing, gross margin, CAC and payback, cohort economics, and the ROI case behind every major spend and product bet.

 - Build the finance operating system. Stand up the tooling, controls, and cadences a real finance function needs. Kill manual work, automate the recurring, and write the playbooks the next finance hires will run on.




WHO YOU ARE

 - 4–8 years of experience across FP&A, corporate finance, investment banking, private equity, or a founding finance role at a high-growth startup, with real hands-on ownership of modeling, close, and reporting

 - Someone with top-tier education in a highly selective and academically rigorous environment and/or experience at top-performing SaaS or AI companies. Advanced degrees are a plus.

title: Regional Manager of Operations, Mid-West Region
description:
As our Regional Manager of Operations, Mid-West , you'll play an important role in supporting and growing a diverse portfolio of emergency, specialty, and urgent care hospitals.
 You'll work directly with Practice Managers, Hospital Administrators, Medical Directors, and veterinary partners to strengthen daily operations, improve financial performance, develop hospital leaders, and create exceptional experiences for clients, patients, and referring veterinarians.
 This role combines hands-on operational leadership with regional business oversight. You'll spend time in hospitals, build relationships with teams, understand the challenges they face, and help develop practical solutions that improve performance.
 You'll also partner closely with our Regional Vice President and central support teams to implement operational initiatives, support hospital growth, and identify opportunities across the region.
 This isn't a role for someone who wants to manage hospitals from behind a spreadsheet. We're looking for someone who enjoys being in the field, coaching leaders, solving problems, and helping teams turn great ideas into measurable results.
 Most importantly, we're looking for a leader who understands that successful hospitals are built through strong relationships, engaged teams, sound business decisions, and consistent execution.
 What You'll Do 
 Lead Regional Hospital Operations 
- Provide operational oversight and support for multiple specialty, emergency, and urgent care hospitals throughout the Mid-West region.
- Partner with hospital leadership to improve daily workflows, staffing efficiency, patient access, and overall operational performance.
- Establish consistent operational expectations while respecting each hospital's unique culture, clinical services, and business needs.
- Identify operational challenges early and work collaboratively with hospital teams to implement sustainable solutions.
- Maintain a strong field presence through regular hospital visits, leadership meetings, and ongoing communication.
 Drive Financial & Business Performance 
- Take ownership of regional financial performance, including revenue growth, EBITDA, labor management, expense control, and profitability.
- Partner with hospital leaders to develop and execute budgets, forecasts, and financial improvement plans.
- Monitor key performance indicators, including revenue, transactions, average transaction charges, labor costs, staffing productivity, and client experience metrics.
- Identify opportunities to improve hospital efficiency, manage expenses, and support sustainable growth.
- Translate financial data into clear, actionable priorities for hospital leadership teams.
 Develop & Empower Hospital Leaders 
- Coach and mentor Practice Managers, Hospital Administrators, and department leaders to strengthen their leadership and business management skills.
- Establish clear expectations, accountability, and consistent follow-through across hospital teams.
- Support leadership development, succession planning, and employee engagement initiatives.
- Partner with Human Resources and Talent Acquisition on recruiting, retention, performance management, and staffing strategies.
- Help hospital leaders navigate challenging conversations, organizational changes, and complex operational situations.
 Support Emergency, Specialty & Urgent Care Operations 
- Understand and support the different staffing, scheduling, workflow, and financial models across emergency, specialty, and urgent care hospitals.
- Partner with medical leadership to improve veterinarian scheduling, clinical support staffing, patient flow, and operational efficiency.
- Identify opportunities to improve appointment availability, service utilization, and access to veterinary care.
- Support hospital teams in managing the operational demands of extended hours, overnight services, and fluctuating caseloads.
- Collaborate with medical leaders to remove operational barriers while respecting clinical decision-making and medical autonomy.
 Strengthen Veterinary Partnerships & Client Experience 
- Build trusted relationships with Medical Directors, veterinary partners, and hospital leadership teams.
- Serve as a reliable operational resource who listens, communicates openly, and follows through on commitments.
- Partner with Marketing and hospital teams to strengthen community awareness, referring veterinarian relationships, and hospital reputation.
- Support initiatives that improve client communication, service accessibility, and the overall client experience.
- Help hospitals identify opportunities for referral growth, client retention, and stronger community relationships.
 Support Regional Growth & Strategic Initiatives 
- Partner with the Regional Vice President to execute regional priorities and operational improvement initiatives.
- Support new hospital integrations, leadership transitions, service expansions, and operational readiness as the region grows.
- Collaborate with Finance, Marketing, Human Resources, Talent Acquisition, IT, and other central support teams to ensure hospitals receive timely and effective support.
- Share best practices across hospitals and contribute to the continued development of our Specialty, Emergency & Urgent Care network.
- Help shape operational processes and leadership resources that support long-term regional growth.

We're looking for an experienced, collaborative leader who understands the business of veterinary medicine and genuinely enjoys helping people succeed.
 Required Experience & Qualifications 
- 5+ years of progressive veterinary hospital operations experience , preferably within emergency, specialty, urgent care, or a combination of these environments.
- 2+ years of multisite leadership experience or comparable senior-level management experience within a large, complex veterinary hospital.
- Demonstrated success improving hospital financial performance, operational efficiency, and team engagement.

- You can work comfortably under minimal direct supervision; note that your manager will be based remotely.

- You give a sh*t – You believe in acting like an owner and making Vital Farms a place to be proud of.

- You can walk in someone else’s boots

title: Strategic Operator
description:
Streaming TV is no longer just a brand awareness channel. It’s becoming a core part of the performance marketing mix, alongside search and social. Vibe.co http://Vibe.co is building the platform that makes TV work like the rest of the acquisition stack: targeted, measurable, and optimized for results.

Vibe.co http://Vibe.co is an Audience First Streaming TV Advertising platform that gives marketers the tools to reach the right audiences, optimize campaigns in real time, and understand what’s actually driving business outcomes. With hyper-targeted segmentation, AI-powered recommendations, real-time optimization, and incrementality measurement, Vibe brings the precision and accountability of digital advertising to the biggest screen in the house.

Today, more than 12,000 brands use Vibe.co http://Vibe.co to reach 120 million+ households. And in August 2026, Vibe.co http://Vibe.co became a Walmart company, opening up a new chapter for the business and the industry. With Walmart’s first-party data and purchase signals now part of the Vibe platform, advertisers can connect TV advertising to real-world transactions and measure the impact of CTV with a level of precision previously associated with platforms like Google and Meta.

This is a unique moment to join Vibe. With Walmart’s scale, data, and reach behind us, we’re building the next generation of TV advertising and creating a more measurable, performance-driven future for the channel.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Vibe is a streaming TV advertising platform, and our biggest projects now touch every team in the company, plus teams at our largest partners. As a Strategic Operator, you’ll work side by side with our leadership team on the company’s most strategic and operational challenges, reporting to our VP of Strategic Initiatives. Right now, these projects have no single owner tracking delivery, sizing impact, and escalating to unblock, so that’s where you come in. Depending on your focus, you’ll partner with our revenue or our technology and product leaders, co-owning high-stakes work and taking new initiatives from first test to a working process. You’ll get real exposure to C-level decision-making and a clear path to grow into leading a team.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own delivery on company-wide projects that span every team at Vibe and our largest partners

 - Align stakeholders across tech, product, and GTM teams on shared priorities

 - Track progress across every workstream so issues surface before they cascade

 - Size the business impact of slippage to guide re-prioritization across teams

 - Escalate blockers to the executive team with a clear recommendation

 - Build the operating cadences that help teams execute high-stakes initiatives consistently

Launch 0→1 initiatives

 - Size the expected impact of new strategic initiatives

 - Build business cases for initiatives that need investment, from ROI models to budget envelopes, in partnership with our BizOps team

 - Test traction on new ideas before they scale

 - Build the operating process that turns a proven concept into a running initiative

 - Shape the team that runs an initiative once it proves out

 - Take full ownership of one initiative within your first six months

Work alongside the leadership team

 - Co-own initiatives with executive leaders, driving the work that makes them land

 - Own special projects that don’t fit a typical job description but are critical to how we scale
   
   


WHAT YOU NEED

 - 4+ years of business-side experience (GTM, growth, chief of staff, or strategic operations), including hands-on time at a hypergrowth or scale-up tech company

 - An engineering or technical foundation, and you’re comfortable getting hands-on: pulling your own data in SQL, building analyses, and prototyping new product ideas with AI tools

 - A track record of landing business-critical, cross-functional projects fast and hands-on: coordinating teams, re-prioritizing, and escalating to unblock

 - Experience leading a 0→1 initiative, including building the process or team behind it

 - Experience moving projects forward with senior leaders and people who didn’t report to you, without needing to be the face of it

 - Hands-on use of AI tools in your daily work, with the ability to explain how they change your output
   
   


NICE TO HAVES

 - A background in strategy consulting or VC, as long as you’ve also operated hands-on in a fast-moving company since

 - Experience in streaming TV advertising, connected TV (CTV), or martech, so you can get up to speed on our business fast

 - Working proficiency in French, helpful for working day to day with our Paris-based leaders and teams




OUR VALUES

At Vibe, we run on three values: Impact, Ambition, and Urgency. We tie every goal to a real business outcome, think 10x rather than settling for good enough, and move daily rather than waiting for perfect conditions.

You'll thrive here if you own outcomes without needing direction, default to action, and hold yourself to results, not effort.

This is a high-performance environment with high-performance rewards: you'll work alongside people who push you, with real ownership over hard problems in a market that's moving fast.

If that sounds like the best version of your career, we want to meet you.

 


WHAT WE OFFER

For candidates in New York, NY, the pay range for this role is $120,000–$230,000.

At Vibe, we want you to build something, own something, and grow fast. Here's how we back that up:

 - Variable pay — Based on real Vibe business goals.

 - Hybrid flexibility — We're in NYC's Flatiron District and our team is in 3x a week!

 - Full health coverage — Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance.

 - 401(k) with matching — We invest in your future, not just your output.

 - Unlimited PTO — Take the time you need. We measure results, not hours.

 - Parental leave — Paid leave for all parents.

 - Annual offsite — The whole team, once a year, somewhere worth the trip.

title: Senior Associate, Business Operations & Analytics
location: New York, New York; Chicago, Illinois; Boston, Massachusetts; San Francisco Bay Area; Remote
description:
About us:

Jerry.ai http://Jerry.ai is a Series C, YC-backed tech startup with 5M+ customers and $240M in funding. Founded in 2017, product launched in 2019, and achieved profitability in 2024.

 

Why we exist:

Your car, home, and motorcycle aren't just purchases, they're the physical embodiment of the life you've worked hard to build. Yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every step of the journey — buying, insuring, maintaining, repairing, selling — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

 

Imagine having a trusted friend in your pocket who takes care of everything: they find you the right car or home at the right price, lock in the best insurance rate without you lifting a finger, remind you before that service appointment turns into an expensive repair, and help you sell at the best price when the time is right. That friend is Jerry.

 

We are building the first AI-powered advisor to manage all your physical assets. We started with your car in 2019, now we’re expanding into new verticals (e.g. home, motorcycle, RV, boat).

 

Why We’re Hiring

Our Business Operations & Analytics  team has been a force multiplier and accelerant to our business that has helped us reach these pivotal milestones in spite of headwinds and within a highly competitive market. They are a team of former McKinsey, BCG and Bain consultants who drive data & insights, and inform decision-making across every corner of our business. They are analytical powerhouses and first principles problem solvers who push forward our most important initiatives across product, growth, tech, and operations.

 

Every business unit has a Business Operations & Analytics team member embedded within it  —  someone who doesn't just run analyses and build dashboards, but shapes what questions we should ask, what data to pull, what conclusions to draw, what decisions to make, and then drives our teams towards our next goal: go from 5M to 50M customers and become a $10B business in the next 4 years. 

 

As our business continues to expand, there is growing demand for more Business Operations & Analytics team members. We are hiring 2-3 people to drive impact in these areas:

 - Growth Marketing 

 - Product Development

 - Strategic Partnerships 

 

On leveling: You may see job ads for this role at different job levels. Our priority is finding the right people, we can be flexible with job title/leveling.

 

Why You Will (Or Won't) Like Working Here

 - No slides: If you've worked in consulting, you know what it feels like to be up at 3am reformatting a deck. That doesn't exist here. The only work that gets done at Jerry is work that will materially change the trajectory of our business — an important product, a new growth channel, a key metric, a critical partner relationship, etc. 

 - No corporate fluff: The Business Operations & Analytics team is 14 insatiable learners who care deeply about solving difficult problems and making a tangible impact. Every person owns a critical domain. There is no bloat, unnecessary meetings, or waiting for approvals. 

 - Hands-on: This is not a pure strategy role, you will also own execution. Your day-to-day will be surfacing analytical insights, driving decisions, and seeing them through end-to-end. 

 

What You'll Own

You'll sit on our central Business Operations & Analytics team but you’ll be embedded in one of Jerry's core business areas — growth, product, AI and automation, strategic partnerships — and own the analytical function for that business unit end-to-end.

 - Define the right problems: Before any analysis, understand what business question it's answering and what decision it will inform. Push back if the question is flawed.

 - Data and insights: Define metrics, build reports, run analyses, design experiments, and surface data insights that move your team's key metrics.

 - Drive outcomes: Bring recommendations to your counterparts in product, growth, finance or operations, tell them what's happening and why, and what next steps should be.

 

Who You Are

 - First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?" 

 - Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.

 - Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.

 

What You'll Bring

 - 2+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.

 - Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.

 - Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.

 - Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.

 

Our Tools

SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.

 
 

While we appreciate your interest and application, due to the volume of applications we receive, only applicants under consideration will be contacted.



Please note: Jerry.ai http://Jerry.ai is only able to hire full-time salaried employees who currently reside in AZ, CA, CO, FL, GA, IL, MA, NC, NJ, NV, NY, OR, TN, TX, UT, VA, or Ontario, Canada, and full-time hourly employees who currently reside in AZ, FL, GA, NV, NY, NC, TN, TX, UT, or VA. title: Lead Economist | Housing
description:
About EliseAI

At EliseAI, we're improving the industries that matter most: housing and healthcare. Everyone needs a place to live and access to quality healthcare, yet both are often harder to secure than they should be. 

By integrating AI agents deeply into existing workflows, we make them more efficient, reduce costs, and improve the experience for everyone.



 - Housing: We simplify how renters tour apartments, sign leases, submit maintenance requests, and stay connected with their property team—bringing everything they need for their home into one place.

 - Healthcare: We make it easy to schedule appointments, complete intake forms, and we help patients communicate with providers, so everyone can focus on health instead of paperwork.
   
   

With EliseAI, organizations reduce manual work, improve accessibility, and deliver a seamless experience across essential services. We recently raised a $350 million https://eliseai.com/blog/intelligence-is-getting-cheaper-life-should-too funding round at a $4 billion valuation led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Bessemer Venture Partners to accelerate this mission.



About The Role

We’re looking for a Lead Economist to build EliseAI’s economics research and market insights function. You’ll transform our proprietary data into benchmarks and compelling narratives that establish EliseAI as the leading authority on housing. You’ll own the full pipeline from raw data to market-shaping insight and serve as EliseAI’s voice on what the numbers mean.



Key Responsibilities

 - Establish EliseAI as the leading authority on rental housing through original research and market insights using our proprietary data.

 - Define and amplify EliseAI’s voice on housing economics across media, industry events, research, and customer channels.

 - Partner with marketing to create high-impact content that strengthens the brand and engages customers.

 - Partner with product and data teams to understand product data, build reliable data pipelines, and create scalable reporting.

 - Expand the reach of EliseAI’s research through partnerships with publications and academic institutions.

 - Use research and thought leadership to strengthen EliseAI’s employer brand, helping attract exceptional talent across the entire company.



Move at rocket speed, build something massive.

We’re scaling fast, solving real client problems with precision and ambition. Here, you own your impact; full autonomy, no micromanagement, no fluff. We hire the best, expect the best, and give you the masterclass of your career. It’s hard, it’s intense, and it’s the most rewarding work you’ll ever do. If you’re hungry, driven, and ready to build something massive, climb aboard.



Requirements

 - 3+ years of experience in insights, data journalism, analytics, economic research, or strategy & operations with a track record of shipping quantitative work for external audiences

 - Exceptional data storytelling: you can turn complex findings into sharp narratives

The role works from established corporate policy and is focused on execution.

- Support inventory control routines at the business units, including physical and cycle count procedures, excess and obsolete reserve calculations, and labor and overhead rate updates.
- Document procedures and retain evidence of control performance so business units can support periodic self-assessments and internal audit requests.
- Maintain the initiative tracker and report status, risks and open items to the Controller and the Manager, ERP Team on a regular cadence.

- 4+ years of experience in business analysis, systems analysis or sales operations, supporting a B2B SaaS go-to-market team.
- Hands-on Salesforce experience and a working understanding of the data model.
- Proven ability to gather business requirements and write user stories and acceptance criteria.
- Experience planning and running UAT and managing releases with a central IT team that owns the platform.
- Fluency in GTM data: pipeline, forecast, bookings and renewals.
- Clear written and verbal communication with both frontline teams and executives.

- Experience with marketing or pipeline attribution.
- Experience with Gong or another revenue intelligence platform.

- Experience using AI tools to speed up analysis, documentation and testing.

- Learn our GTM stack, the Salesforce data model and Salesforce IT’s release process.
- Meet your key stakeholders in Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Renewals and Deal Desk.

- Build connections with members from other teams through active networking and community building.
- Run intake and a standing cadence with Salesforce IT, and ship your first release end to end with stories, UAT and field communications.
- Document the requirements baseline and evaluation criteria for CPQ.
- Audit current attribution gaps and agree on requirements with Marketing and Sales leadership.

ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As Senior Manager of FP&A at Fluidstack, you will be a cornerstone of our Finance leadership team, owning the financial planning, analysis, and decision-support infrastructure that powers one of the fastest-moving companies in AI. You will lead the full FP&A function — from annual planning and budgeting to long-range financial modeling, scenario analysis, and board-level reporting — all while building processes from the ground up. This is a high-impact, high-ownership role for someone who thrives in ambiguity, moves with urgency, and understands that great FP&A is as much about influencing decisions as it is about accuracy.



You will partner deeply with Engineering, Operations, Sales, and Finance to translate business strategy into financial clarity, and you will be instrumental in preparing Fluidstack for the next phase of its growth.

 - Own Fluidstack’s annual operating plan, quarterly forecasting cycles, and long-range financial model across all business units and geographies.

 - Build and lead a world-class FP&A team, establishing the infrastructure, cadence, and culture of financial rigor the business needs to scale.

 - Partner with executive leadership team to develop and pressure-test strategic financial scenarios, capital allocation decisions, and growth investments.

 - Drive board and investor reporting — translating complex operational data into clear, compelling financial narratives.

 - Embed FP&A as a true business partner across Engineering, Operations, Sales, and Finance — owning the P&L bridge and variance analysis end-to-end.

 - Lead IPO readiness efforts from an FP&A perspective, including development of public-company-grade financial reporting processes and controls.

 - Own the build-out of FP&A systems and tooling, including integration with ERP platforms (NetSuite) and data infrastructure.

 - Develop KPI frameworks and financial performance dashboards that give leadership real-time visibility into business health.




BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

 - 10+ years of progressive FP&A experience, including prior experience in a senior leadership role.

 - Proven track record building and leading FP&A functions at high-growth technology, infrastructure, or pre-IPO companies.

 - Deep expertise in financial modeling, budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning in complex, multi-entity environments.

 - Experience partnering directly with C-suite and board-level stakeholders on financial strategy and reporting.

 - Strong command of ERP systems; NetSuite proficiency required.

 - Demonstrated ability to hire, develop, and lead high-performing finance teams.

 - Exceptional communication skills — you can distill complex financial data into clear insights for both technical and non-technical audiences.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; CPA or CFA preferred.

 - Prior exposure to IPO readiness, S-1 preparation, or public company financial reporting standards.

 - Familiarity with multi-currency and multi-jurisdictional financial environments.

 - Experience implementing or scaling FP&A tooling and systems in partnership with engineering or data teams.

 - Big 4 or investment banking background as a complement to industry experience.

The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City.

Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. Your Team:
The Office of Housing Access and Stability (“HAS”) consists of the divisions of Housing Opportunity, Tenant and Owner Resources, Housing Stability, Budget and Program Operations, and Program Policy and Innovation. The Office provides subsidies, placement services, and tools that connect New Yorkers to affordable housing and ensures vulnerable households in subsidized housing have the support they need to be safely housed. Housing Access is committed to expanding housing choices, affirmatively furthering fair housing, and stabilizing the financial health of buildings.

We are partnering with a U.S.-based technology company building advanced AI systems focused on financial modeling and decision-making.

Minimum 2 years of full-time, paid finance experience after graduation. Internships, training programs and course projects do not count. This role is not suitable for students or recent graduates.

 


ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

The goal of this project is to train AI to think like real financial professionals: how models are built from scratch, how assumptions are structured, and how credit and debt decisions are made using financial models.

 

This is a hands-on Excel modeling role where you will build detailed credit and debt models from a blank spreadsheet and explain your logic. We prioritize candidates who can build full models end-to-end and explain why a model works, rather than just producing summary dashboards or tweaking templates.

 

We evaluate two distinct technical tracks under this posting:

 - Model and link 3-statement borrower financials, amortization schedules, payment-in-kind (PIK) interest, dynamic cash sweeps, DSCR, and debt covenants (Credit track).

 - This role is NOT: An internal corporate finance, FP&A, or deal-structuring role; it does not involve loan administration, retail collections, or client presentations.

 - You rely on pre-formatted templates, third-party calculators, or add-ins to build your models.
   
    

 - Your modeling background comes primarily from academic courses, financial modeling bootcamps, or case studies rather than professional employment.
   
    

 - You are currently seeking a part-time role or cannot commit to ~40 hours per week.
   
    


WHY JOIN?

title: Business Analyst - Health Insurance
description:
Accountabilities
As Business Analyst, you will act as the link between business departments and IT teams, ensuring that insurance requirements are accurately understood, documented, and translated into practical solutions. Your responsibilities will include:
- 
 Analyze business requirements and operational processes within the Swiss health and accident insurance sector.
- 
 Develop appropriate solutions in collaboration with business stakeholders and IT specialists.
- 
 Manage requirements throughout the full lifecycle, including analysis, concept development, specification, implementation, and validation.
- 
 Contribute to the continuous improvement of insurance applications and business processes, particularly claims processing and automated invoice verification.
- 
 Ensure the functional and technical quality of applications, supporting error analysis and resolution when needed.
- 
 Configure and maintain insurance applications, including keeping reference data and tariff information accurate and up to date.
- 
 Participate in customer projects and coordinate release planning and implementation with customers, business teams, developers, and system providers.
- 
 Monitor legislative and regulatory developments in the Swiss insurance market and identify the resulting business and system requirements.
 Requirements
 The ideal candidate combines a solid understanding of health insurance operations with strong business analysis and requirements engineering capabilities. You should be comfortable working independently while collaborating with a range of business and technical stakeholders. The following qualifications are expected:
- 
 Degree or professional training in business informatics, computer science, or a commercial discipline, supported by strong IT affinity.
- 
 Several years of professional experience in the Swiss health and/or accident insurance sector.
- 
 In-depth knowledge of claims processes under the Swiss Health Insurance Act (KVG) and/or Insurance Contract Act (VVG).
- 
 Experience with insurance tariffs and tariff-related processes is an advantage.
- 
 Proven experience in business analysis, requirements engineering, and the analysis, design, and specification of business requirements.
- 
 Familiarity with insurance applications, ideally Adcubum Syrius or Sumex.
- 
 Experience configuring applications; knowledge of SQL is an advantage.
- 
 Knowledge of software testing, quality assurance, or release management is a plus.
- 
 Independent, structured, and solution-oriented working style.
- 
 Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with different stakeholders.
- 
 Excellent written and spoken German, with a professional communication style.

- 
 Remote working arrangement, open to candidates worldwide.

 Fixed-term employment contract.

 Opportunity to contribute to projects within the Swiss health and accident insurance sector.

 Potential to work across business analysis, insurance application optimization, and IT implementation.

-

-

title: Senior Manager, Business Operations
description:
About the Role

Clutch is at a pivotal moment. We're growing significantly year over year, and we need more connective tissue to keep pace. We're hiring a Senior Manager, Business Operations to connect the commercial side of the house, so the teams that win, onboard, and retain our customers work from the same facts and toward the same goals. This role sits in Finance.

This is a people manager role. You'll lead our Revenue Operations (RevOps) team and act as an operating partner to senior leaders across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Implementation, People, and Finance. Together with the RevOps team, you own the shared language of the business (definitions, data, and processes) so commercial teams make decisions from one view of it.

When something important doesn't have an owner yet, it lands with you: a partnership strategy, a new commercial model, or pricing and margin guidance for leadership. This is a fast-moving startup. We're building toward a much larger company but we aren't one yet, and most of this role has no playbook. You'll define the process, build the tool, and hand it to the team. If you want established structure, this likely isn't the role.

About the Team

You'll report to the Director of Business Operations and work directly with senior leaders across the company as a neutral partner to every function rather than an advocate for one. Your work will be visible, and it will significantly influence how we make commercial decisions.

You'll lead a small, high-ownership RevOps team that runs the systems and data our commercial teams depend on, and creates leverage for them to do their jobs even better. The team doesn't just own systems. They build automation, tooling, and processes, and they're close partners to Sales and Marketing. You'll coach them, set priorities, and open up more strategic scope, while giving them real autonomy.



What You’ll Do

Within 3 months, you will:

 - Learn the business end to end: the revenue funnel, the customer lifecycle, how each commercial team works day to day, and where decisions get stuck

 - Build trust with your RevOps team: learn the work they own, and set priorities and team rhythms together

 - Deliver the first version of client-level margin and cost-to-serve, the analysis that grounds our pricing strategy

 - Develop a first point of view on pricing and packaging for revenue leadership, built on that analysis

 - Put AI to work in your own workflow from week one, and identify the first set of manual, repetitive processes across the commercial teams worth automating

Within 6 months, you will:

 - Stand up a first version of a deal desk, including an approval workflow, pricing and discount guardrails, and standard commercial terms

 - Partner with Sales and Marketing leaders as they prepare for the monthly business review: pressure-test their plans and point out risks, then solve them with the RevOps team by creating new processes, tooling, or automation

 - Build on the strength of the RevOps team: prioritize its roadmap against business outcomes and take on more strategic work together

 - Launch your first AI-enabled workflows or automations that remove manual reporting or reconciliation for the commercial teams, with time saved tracked

Within 9 months, you will:

 - Have a team whose output and standards hold, with the processes, tooling, and automation you've built running without you in the room

 - Have AI-enabled, self-serve tooling that commercial teams use day to day, with measurable time savings

 - Be the person leadership trusts to pick up the next important thing that doesn't have an owner yet



What You’ll Bring

 - 5-8 years of total experience that combines consulting or banking with time as an operator inside a company

 - Experience managing people: you've coached ICs, given direct feedback, made tough talent calls, and built team rhythms

 - Startup experience. You've worked in a fast-moving, ever-changing environment where structure wasn't already there, and you built it. This is not a role for someone whose experience is only at large, established enterprises.

 - Strong analytical and financial modeling skills, including forecasting. You're very comfortable building models in spreadsheets from scratch, and they hold up to scrutiny. You use AI to move faster and sharpen your work, and you have the foundational modeling knowledge to know when its output is wrong.

 - Data-first and self-sufficient. You open the dataset before you build the slide, you're always looking for more data to test an idea, and you're comfortable getting into raw data yourself. You use AI to analyze it faster and know enough to check its work.

 - Commercial acumen: you can read commercial terms, spot the problematic ones, and reason about pricing, discounting, margin, and deal structure

 - A clear communicator who can walk an executive through a messy problem and leave them with a decision, and who is just as effective working alongside an AE, a CSM, or an engineer

 - Comfort with ambiguity. When something isn't set up yet, your instinct is to build it, not to wait for it. You create structure, manage competing priorities, and pivot when things change.

 - Relentless follow-through: you close loops, and people stop checking on what you've said you'll do

 - A partner's temperament: you challenge constructively without taking sides, you surface problems early, and you resolve cross-team conflict without escalating it

Nice-to-haves:

 - Industry experience in fintech, financial services, lending, banking, or credit unions

 - An MBA (not required)

Please note that this role may evolve as our business needs change, so we appreciate your flexibility and adaptability.

What’s In It For You?

 - Remote Flexibility: Enjoy the freedom of remote work from anywhere, balancing life and career seamlessly.

 - Unforgettable Off-Sites: Twice a year, bond with colleagues in exciting destinations, fostering teamwork and fresh ideas.

 Our Culture

 Atlas is seeking a strategic and relationship-driven professional to support the firm's growth through capital structure strategy and investor engagement. Who we are 
 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. 
 About the team 
 Stripe’s Tax Transfer Pricing team designs, implements, and defends the intercompany pricing policies that support Stripe’s global operating model, ensuring pricing between Stripe entities is compliant, defensible, and aligned with how the business creates value.
 As Stripe expands its product portfolio and international footprint, our transfer pricing policies and documentation must evolve alongside the business. Transactions between Stripe affiliates are becoming increasingly complex and, in some cases, share characteristics with transactions commonly undertaken by financial services institutions. These arrangements, including those supporting Stripe’s stablecoin-related activities, may also be subject to scrutiny from regulators that oversee the financial services sector. We are seeking an experienced Transfer Pricing Specialist with financial services expertise to help develop practical, scalable transfer pricing policies, work through the tax and regulatory considerations relevant to intercompany arrangements, and provide subject matter expertise in audit defense and dispute resolution.
 What you’ll do 
 The Financial Services Transfer Pricing Strategist will be a hands-on, collaborative member of the team responsible for developing and implementing compliant, practical transfer pricing policies and processes. The role will focus on transactions between Stripe’s legal entities that have characteristics commonly associated with the financial services sector, including intercompany arrangements supporting Stripe’s stablecoin-related activities.
 This individual will work closely with teams across the organization and must be an excellent communicator who can explain complex transfer pricing concepts clearly to non-tax audiences. - Build relationships with product and business leaders to understand their organizational structure and activities, and adapt transfer pricing policies in response to changes
- Assist finance, legal, and tax teams in government and regulatory audits, and support Stripe’s participation in tax audits, advance pricing agreements, and competent authority proceedings

description:
Precision for Medicine is looking for a Site Contracts and Budget Manager to join our European Team. The position can be fully remote from Poland, Slovakia, Serbia, Romania, or Hungary. 
 Position Summary: 
 The primary focus of this role is global clinical trial budget template development . You will be responsible for translating complex clinical trial protocols and study documentation into accurate, comprehensive, and negotiation-ready global/site budget templates across multiple countries. Demonstrated hands-on experience developing investigator/site budget templates for global, sponsor- or CRO-managed clinical trials is required. 
 The role will also include reviewing, drafting, negotiation and tracking of a variety of legal agreements including confidentiality agreements, master confidentiality agreements, clinical study agreements and amendment agreements.  You will work closely with Clinical Operations study team and play a key role to ensure deliverables are in alignment with defined study timelines.
 Essential functions of the job include but are not limited to: 
 Global Clinical Trial Budget Template Development – Primary Responsibility: 
- 
 Review clinical trial protocols, including amendments, SoAs, manuals, and other study documentation to identify all activities with potential site-level cost implications.

-

- 
 Ensure budget structures support appropriate payment terms and CTA exhibits.
- 
 Incorporate approved country-specific cost information and available benchmarks into global and country-level budget templates.
- 
 Establish proposed negotiation targets, parameters, and escalation pathways.
- 
 Perform detailed QC of budget templates before release to assigned SCM negotiators, including verification of formulas, visit totals, conditional procedures, invoiceable items, and patient-cost calculations.
- 
 Confirm consistency between protocol/SoA requirements and completed budgets and clearly document budget assumptions and negotiation parameters.
- 
 Maintain version control and an auditable record of budget-development decisions.
- 
 Review protocol amendments and revised study documents to identify financial impact and update master/site budget templates accordingly.
- 
 Clearly identify added, removed, or modified procedures and associated financial impacts for SCM.
- 
 Serve as a budget-development SME for SCM and study teams and clarify budget assumptions and unusual protocol requirements.
- 
 Support continuous improvement and standardization of global budget templates, tools, SOPs, work instructions, and training.
- 
 Identify opportunities for automation and increased efficiency in clinical trial budget development.
 Site Contracts – Secondary Responsibility 
- Review, draft and negotiate a variety of agreements including master services agreements, site contracts, consulting agreements, vendor agreements, confidentiality agreements, and other client contracts.
- Work with supervisor and various internal/external key stakeholders to resolve/escalate contractual issues.
- Ensure adherence to company policies, procedures and contracting standards.
- Update relevant study team members regarding the status of contract negotiations and execution.
- Establish, track, report and manage site contract metrics.

title: Pricing Analyst
description:
About the Company:



Industrious is the largest premium workplace-as-a-service provider and home to the highest-rated workplaces in the industry. Everything we do comes down to creating great days for teams of all sizes and stages, including our own. We’re looking for people who love thinking outside the box and thrive in a truly collaborative setting. As teammates, we encourage new ideas and toast every win. Great days also start when everyone can be their authentic self at work. Industrious is committed to creating an inclusive, respectful environment that embraces your individuality and quirkiness. You are valued for who YOU are. To learn more, visit www.industriousoffice.com/careers http://www.industriousoffice.com/careers.




PRICING ANALYST (REVENUE MANAGEMENT)


Industrious is the largest premium flexible workspace company in the world, operating over 250 locations across 10 countries as part of the CBRE portfolio. We design workplaces where teams feel welcomed, supported, and able to do their best work. The same principle guides how we work together as a company.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Right now, the pricing judgment for Industrious's existing North America private office portfolio sits with one person who has built deep expertise in it: knowing which renewals need a bump, which office needs a promotion instead of a price cut, and which market is quietly slipping. That person is moving on to bigger things, and we need someone to step into that seat, formalize what works, and keep roughly 200 price changes a month running accurately, on time, and grounded in real conversations with the General Managers who run our buildings.


This is a Pricing Analyst, Revenue Management role, reporting into the pricing team. You will own business-as-usual pricing execution for the existing North America private office portfolio, with the scope to grow into other products and regions as the team expands.




WHAT MIGHT YOUR DAY LOOK LIKE

You start the morning scanning the pricing dashboard and notice a suite at 1411 Broadway that hasn't sold in weeks, while the identical suite next door is occupied at full list price. The GM has asked for a price cut. You pull the tour and application data, see it's a single-unit problem rather than a market problem, and decide a one-month promotion makes more sense than dropping the list price and setting up a harder renewal conversation down the road.



By mid-morning, you are on the phone with a GM in Nashville, walking through why an entire category of seven-to-nine person offices isn't moving. You ask about tour volume, application quality, and whether the floor plans still fit what people are searching for. You leave the call with a plan, and the GM leaves it feeling like someone actually looked at their building, not just their numbers.



In the afternoon, you work through the week's renewal batch, running each one against the pricing logic the team uses to decide what gets pushed through and what needs a second look. You flag one segment where occupancy has slipped two months running, log it for deeper review, and jot down a note on the decision tree so the next person doesn't have to relearn it from scratch.



You close the day updating the system with the changes you've made, checking your numbers against the portfolio report, and sending a short note to your manager on the one call that needs a decision above your pay grade.




WHAT YOU WILL OWN

 - Execute accurate, on-schedule pricing changes across roughly 200 price adjustments a month on the existing portfolio

 - Diagnose underperforming units or segments through variance analysis and turn findings into concrete pricing recommendations

 - Build direct, trusted relationships with General Managers as their first call on pricing, not a name behind a ticket

 - Run the renewal process end to end, from sending renewals to recommending pricing based on account and market performance

 - Evaluate the return on past promotional campaigns to shape smarter promotional decisions going forward

 - Keep pricing platforms, algorithms, and databases configured and accurate as the portfolio and product line grow

 - Document pricing logic and decision processes so institutional knowledge stops living in one person's head

 - Report on key revenue metrics, including Price/Seat, Occupancy, and RevPAR, for commercial leadership
   
   

This role leans on Problem Solving, because variance analysis only matters if you can turn a pattern in the data into a clear recommendation. It leans just as heavily on Communication, because the GMs you work with need to hear from a real person, not just see a system update. And it runs on Ownership and Bias for Action: at 200 changes a month, you move decisions forward with the information you have rather than waiting for certainty.

Industrious forecasts revenue across a global network of flexible workspace locations, and the next step is making that forecasting predictive rather than reactive, while building equally strong visibility into the sales pipeline that feeds it. That is the challenge this role exists to solve.



As Manager, Commercial Analytics, based in New York and reporting into Commercial Strategy & Analytics leadership, you will own the models, data, and narrative that let Finance and commercial leadership see what is coming before it shows up in the numbers. title: Real Estate Associate
description:
About the Company:

Industrious is the largest premium workplace-as-a-service provider and home to the highest-rated workplaces in the industry. Everything we do comes down to creating great days for teams of all sizes and stages, including our own. We believe that what makes a great day at work is the people on your team and the problems you get to solve together. We’re looking for people who love thinking outside the box and thrive in a truly collaborative setting. As teammates, we encourage new ideas and toast every win. We’re excited about having a meaningful impact on people’s workplace experience.



Great days also start when everyone can be their authentic self at work. Diversity of backgrounds, thoughts, and ideas is critical to our success in delivering great workplace experiences, both for our members and for each other. Industrious is committed to creating an inclusive, respectful environment that embraces your individuality and quirkiness. You are valued for who YOU are. We celebrate our people as individuals who can accomplish great things when we work together as one team.



To learn more, visit www.industriousoffice.com/careers http://www.industriousoffice.com/careers.



About the Role

Industrious signs new landlord partnerships every year, and the number is growing as our business development team expands. Before any of those deals move forward, someone has to check that it holds together: that the assumptions are sound, that the start date, budgets, rent, pricing, and returns all track, and that the figures from design and construction have carried through correctly. As a Real Estate Associate on our Real Estate Transactions team that will be your job!



You will underwrite assigned deals in Excel, explain what drives their returns, and flag where a deal is tight, whether on pricing, occupancy, or CapEx. Our business development colleagues make the call on whether a deal goes ahead, and your analysis is what they rely on to make it well. You will work with Design, Construction, Finance, and other teams to make sure every number is right, supporting several business development colleagues as deal flow shifts.



Our approach to underwriting is different from a traditional real estate shop, and we will teach it to you. In your first few months you will get close review and clear guidance while you learn how we work. You will also join at a good time: the team is growing, new roles are being added, and we are underwriting a new product, so there is real room to learn, ask questions, and grow with us.



Success here means accurate work. The team trusts your numbers, your flags are clear, and any mistake you make happens once, not twice.



What Might Your Day Look Like

Your morning starts with a new deal from one of our business development colleagues. You go through the model piece by piece: the start date, the budget, the rent and revenue share assumptions, the cash flows, the IRR, and the margin the location is expected to earn per rentable square foot. The returns look fine at first, but pricing is tighter than it seems, so you note it clearly with the number that would need to change.



Late morning, updated figures arrive from Design and Construction. You check that they have flowed into the model correctly. One CapEx figure does not match the construction budget, so you confirm the right number with the construction team before it goes any further.



In the afternoon, you walk your business development colleague through the deal: what the returns look like, where the risk sits, and which assumptions matter most. They decide what happens next. Then priorities shift, and another colleague needs support on a deal heading to Investment Committee, so you move over and check that every figure in the review material ties back to the underwriting.



Before you wrap up, you update your trackers and checklists so the team knows where every deal you are supporting stands.



What You Will Own

 - Underwrite assigned deals in Excel, checking every assumption and making sure each component, from start date and budgets to pricing and IRR, tracks.

 - Explain each deal's returns clearly, including IRR, cash flows, P&L, and margin, so business development can make an informed decision.

 - Flag where a deal is tight, on pricing, occupancy, CapEx, OpEx, rent, or revenue share, and where it may need more support.

 - Make sure figures from Design, Construction, and Finance carry through accurately into the deal.

 - Support deal reviews and Investment Committee materials with numbers that hold up to scrutiny.

 - Support several business development colleagues across their deal flow, moving between priorities as needs change.

title: Business Operations Generalist, Finance & Accounting
description:
ABOUT WONDERLY

Wonderly is a closed-loop, end-to-end system that self-improves on our customers’ revenue. We serve the home service industry ($1.3T), and can consistently double a new customer’s revenue within 90 days. We make all of our AI and software completely free - and only get paid when our customers make real money. We’re here helping real small businesses make a life, pay for their children’s college tuition, and live the American dream.

Pre-AI SaaS sold tools. AI companies claim they sell outcomes - task done, call answered, lead booked, ticket resolved - but calls or leads aren’t the outcomes that ultimately matter. Revenue is what ultimately matters, and today, none of the AI companies actually promise revenue. Wonderly changes that.

Our 70-person team (mostly in PDE) spent over a year building in stealth; our thesis is that - if you actually want to control the end result (revenue) of a business and deploy AI fast/cheaply, you can’t just build the sexy part (agents), you must also build the unsexy parts and own everything end to end: the system of record layer and the application layer. We built from scratch every software a home service business needs - replacing ServiceTitan, Squarespace, Ringcentral, Jobber, Square, Hubspot, and a dozen others applications. And we built every agent necessary - AI marketing, AI receptionist, AI voice, AI sales outreach, AI sales coaching, AI follow-ups, AI 3D design, AI finance, AI quoting, AI collections, and more - all embedded inside our own system with native data access. As a result, we can deploy dozens of production-ready Agents to our customers in under 24 hours with no FDEs, no integrations, and no data cleaning work.

We are the most outcome driven business model in the business because we’ve proven our system and AI Agents actually work in driving the end result - revenue. We are not trying to sell our customers a dream - each of our 10+ core AI Agents help improve our customers’ revenue by 5-20%.

Wonderly already has PMF and has gone from 0 → 1 (we are happy to share more over a call), with very clear moat and deep industry knowledge that took a team of 70 hardcore A-players 18 months to build (we are at least 2 years ahead of anyone else in the space). We believe Wonderly has the potential to be a $100B - $1T outcome. The market is massive https://www.acquired.fm/episodes/home-depot: home service businesses across North America (a $1.3T market). We’ve raised over $50M from top-tier investors, have $20M a year in free cashflow from another product line (Motion), and all that money gets pumped into Wonderly.




ABOUT THE HIRING MANAGER

Hi, I’m Harry, Wonderly’s CEO. 

You’ll report directly to me, and you’ll work closely with our CTO, Chander, to build a scalable AI finance & operations system. I’m looking for someone I can trust to own the operational details that keep Wonderly running, from getting the numbers right to working through a vendor contract or fixing a broken process.

You don’t need to have seen every problem before. You do need to ask good questions, exercise sound judgment, and follow through. As you build context and earn trust, you’ll take on more ownership across the business.

 


THE ROLE

We’re hiring someone to own the financial and business operations behind Wonderly.

Accounting is roughly a third of the role. You’ll make sure vendors get paid correctly, coordinate month-end close with our external accountants, and keep tax requirements and financial systems organized. The rest spans contracts, procurement, insurance, equity administration, and the operational problems that come with a growing company.

We want someone with an accounting foundation who wants broad business ownership. You should be comfortable investigating an unfamiliar charge, working through a vendor renewal, coordinating with outside counsel, and building a process so the same issue is easier next time.

Your responsibilities will include:

 - Accounting operations: Validate invoices, collect vendor documentation, coordinate approvals, and schedule payments.

 - Month-end close: Keep close notes, provide supporting information to our accountants, investigate discrepancies, and flag unusual transactions.

 - Tax coordination: Keep filings, registrations, notices, and year-end reporting moving with our external providers.

 - Financial systems: Maintain tools such as Stripe, Subscript, Hubifi, and QuickBooks as the business changes.

 - Contracts and procurement: Coordinate agreements with business owners and counsel, negotiate vendor terms, and track commitments and renewals.

 - Corporate operations: Manage insurance renewals, routine equity administration, corporate records, registrations, and incoming notices.

 - Process improvement: Document recurring work, establish clear owners and deadlines, and work with our internal team to automate repetitive tasks.

You’ll have recurring responsibilities and unexpected problems. You’re accountable for closing the loop on both.




WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE DIFFERENT

You’ll report to our CEO, work closely with our CTO, and see how decisions get made across the company.

Your accounting knowledge will give you a starting point, but your scope will extend across finance, legal, procurement, and corporate operations. You’ll work with accountants, lawyers, brokers, vendors, and internal teams—and be responsible for making sure work gets finished.

You’ll also have room to improve how the company operates. When something takes ten manual steps, we want you to question it, understand the constraints, and help build a better system.

As you become someone the company trusts with increasingly complex problems, your responsibilities can grow with you.




BACKGROUNDS THAT TEND TO WORK

People from these backgrounds could thrive here:

 - Accounting or finance operations at a fast-growing startup.

 - Public accounting with hands-on exposure to startup clients.

 - Business operations roles with me

title: Finance & Operations Analyst
description:
ABOUT BASELAYER 
 Every business in America needs a bank account to exist. The system that decides whether they're real, who's behind them, and whether they're a risk, runs on infrastructure from the 1980s. We're rebuilding that layer from scratch.
 Baselayer is the identity layer for institutions across the United States: the most complete business graph in America and every human tied to it. We fuse public records, IRS data, sanctions lists, web signals, and fraud telemetry from 2,200+ financial institutions into a single graph that resolves any business and the humans behind it in milliseconds. The legacy credit bureaus took 50 years to build something that gets 60% match rates. We've built something that gets 98% in under two years.
 Today we're trusted by over 20% of financial institutions in America including FIS, Rho, Socure and top five US banks. But the graph is becoming infrastructure for anyone who needs to know if a business is real and worth trusting: gig platforms, marketplaces, AI companies, and commerce infrastructure at scale.
 Trust is the substrate of every financial transaction. We're rebuilding it.
 ABOUT THE TEAM 
 AI agents are starting to transact: opening accounts, buying services, moving money on behalf of the businesses and people behind them. Every one of those transactions has a counterparty asking the question banks have always asked: who am I dealing with, and can I trust them? Today's identity infrastructure wasn't built to answer it at agent speed.
 The Agentic Economy team is extending Baselayer's business graph into the trust layer for agentic commerce: verifiable credentials that bind an agent to the verified business and human behind it, a registry counterparties can query in real time, and verification APIs that plug into the networks, platforms, and protocols where agent transactions happen.
 We run like a startup inside a startup: a small senior team led by our GM of Agentic Economy, working directly with payment networks, banks, wallet providers, and agent platforms. The category is being defined right now; the standards, seats, and infrastructure decisions of the next 18 months will be consequential for a decade.
 ABOUT THE ROLE 
 We are looking for a Finance & Operations Analyst to be the Swiss Army knife of our Operations & Finance team. You will own the numbers — month-end close, accounting, and FP&A — and you will also own smaller tasks that keep a fast-growing startup running, from office logistics to getting a new teammate's laptop set up.
 This is a highly visible role reporting directly to the Head of Operations & Finance. You will see the entire business: how revenue is recognized, where money goes, what it costs to grow, and where the process is still held together with duct tape. Your job is to close the books accurately, build the reporting leadership relies on, and then go fix the duct tape.
 This is not a role for someone who wants a narrow lane. We are looking for someone who is willing to get their hands dirty, moves fast, and takes as much pride in a clean reconciliation as in unblocking a teammate on a Friday afternoon.
 WHAT YOU'LL DO 
 FP&A & Reporting

- Produce recurring management and board-level reporting on revenue, burn, runway, and departmental spend

 Business Operations

- Own vendor and software spend management, including renewals and contracts
- Support compliance and corporate housekeeping in partnership with Legal and Compliance including annual SOC2, penetration testing, business insurance and more

- Jump on ad-hoc projects across the business wherever the need is greatest

The Policy Lead will own the policy substance of the plan.  Policy Design 
- Lead development of the AI economic plan, from first framework to final proposals
- Identify the plan's key choice points and lay out clear, realistic options for each, including trade-offs, costs, and precedents
- Draw on existing research and proposals on automation, labor markets, the social safety net, workforce training, tax policy, and competition
- Draft policy memos, option papers, and the plan itself
 Working with the Research Team 
- Turn policy options into concrete proposals our research team can test with voters through polling and message testing
- Work through the plan's choice points with the research team, and use results to refine the plan based on what is popular, what is persuasive, and what is sound policy

- Pragmatic: You care about policy that works and can also pass
- Collaborative: You work well across disciplines and welcome having your ideas tested against evidence

- Experience with polling, message testing, or survey research

 What We Offer

- Impact: You will shape a concrete plan for how the country handles one of the biggest economic shifts in generations, grounded in what the public actually wants
 About Blue Rose Research 
 Blue Rose Research builds data and AI tools that help Democrats win elections. Our team combines engineering, data science, and political strategy to power decisions for the country's top campaigns and progressive organizations. We forecast elections, test ads, and use generative AI to help campaigns understand what's happening in the news and respond fast with messages that actually work. We have guided how hundreds of millions of dollars are spent in modern campaigns. We're a small, mission-driven team that builds fast, experiments boldly, and helps progressives communicate and win—guided by curiosity, purpose, and a genuine desire to use technology for good.
