title: Senior Finance Business Partner
description:
WHO WE ARE

At Trustly, we're building a smarter, faster and more secure financial future by revolutionizing the world of payments. As a global leader in Open Banking Payments, we are establishing Pay by Bank as the new standard at checkout, providing unparalleled freedom, speed and ease to millions of consumers and merchants worldwide.

Our Ambition: To build the world's most disruptive payment network and redefine what the payment experience should feel like.

Trustly is a global team of innovators, collaborators and doers. If you are driven by a strong sense of purpose and thrive in a dynamic, entrepreneurial and high growth environment, join us and be part of a team that's transforming the way the world pays.



ABOUT THE ROLE

This is an opportunity for an experienced finance business partner to join our Commercial Finance team, based in our London office. You will own the COGS profit and loss line (bank fees and hosting costs) and the unit economics across the cost base, partnering closely with Banking, Infrastructure and Engineering to control and improve margins. You will lead monthly performance commentary and the annual planning process for the cost base, working closely with Accounting and the wider business.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - COGS & Unit Economics: Own the COGS P&L line end to end (bank fees and hosting costs) and the unit economics across the cost base, including cost per transaction, feeding into merchant pricing models and investment cases.

 - Banking Partnerships: Partner with the VP Banking Relationships on banking partnerships, driving down banking costs and identifying bank routing efficiencies, including modelling the aggregator versus direct integration breakeven.

 - Cloud Economics: Partner with the VP Infrastructure on cloud cost analysis, ensuring infrastructure spend scales efficiently with usage.

 - Engineering Partnership: Partner with the VP Engineering on capacity allocation and capitalised development project decisions, day to day rather than at a distance.

 - Performance Commentary: Own monthly performance commentary on COGS, working with Accounting to confirm reported numbers are accurate and with the business to understand what is driving the trajectory.

 - Annual Planning: Lead the annual planning process for the cost base, including banking negotiation support, bank routing efficiencies and cloud or hosting optimisation as key initiatives, then support the business through the year to track performance against plan and course correct.

 - Investment decision support: Build business cases for high impact initiatives, which could include new products, regulatory permission changes in key markets, particularly in Europe, and support new product development with ad hoc financial analysis.
   
   

QUALIFICATIONS

The successful candidate will have:

 - 5+ years of experience in FP&A, commercial finance or a similar finance business partnering role;

 - Strong stakeholder management experience, comfortable partnering with finance and non finance teams, including engineering, banking and infrastructure partners;

 - Strong analytical capability, with experience building financial models and business cases;

 - Proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets for modelling and analysis;

 - Experience improving processes and ways of working, including bringing automation into finance reporting or planning, is a plus.
   
   

WHAT WE OFFER

At Trustly, you will have the chance to solve meaningful challenges alongside some of the brightest minds in FinTech. Together, we are shaping the future of payments in an environment that celebrates curiosity, collaboration and innovation. You will be challenged and empowered to grow, making a real impact every step of the way.

Our team is as diverse as the global footprint we serve. At Trustly, we foster a workplace where everyone feels they belong, a place where teamwork thrives, ideas flourish and we never forget to have fun along the way. We are proud and committed to being an Equal Opportunity Employer and believe an open and inclusive environment enables people to do their best work.



OUR FANTASTIC BENEFITS

 - 25 days of holiday to support a healthy work life balance;

 - Monthly team outing allowance to enjoy social events with your colleagues;

 - Parental leave top up, additional support for new parents;

 - Daily breakfast and on site perks to make your workday smoother;

 - Wellbeing support, our health allowance covers gym memberships, massages and much more to help you feel your best;

 - PLUS additional benefits designed to enhance your work life experience!
   
   

SHAPE YOUR ROLE AND MAKE AN IMPACT

Join a dynamic environment where you can take ownership, drive change and continuously embrace new challenges. We're looking for dedicated and highly motivated individuals who thrive in a fast paced environment and enjoy collaborating across different areas of the organisation.

Healthcare is in crisis and the people behind the results deserve better. With more and more data coming from wearables, lab tests, and patient–doctor interactions, we’re entering an era where data is abundant.

Junction is building the infrastructure layer for diagnostic healthcare, making patient data accessible, actionable, and automated across labs and devices. Our mission is simple but ambitious: build the infrastructure that makes predictive, personalized care possible.

If you're passionate about how technology can supercharge healthcare, you’ll fit right in.

Backed by Creandum, Point Nine, 20VC, YC, and leading angels, we’re working to solve one of the biggest challenges of our time: making healthcare personalized, proactive, and affordable. We’re already connecting millions and scaling fast.





WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS, AND WHY NOW

Junction is a highly analytical business. Our growth depends on understanding the economics of our products, customers, and operations, and using that understanding to make better decisions about where to invest and how to scale.

Today, much of that work happens directly with our founder and across individual teams. As we grow, we need someone who can bring it together, establish a clear financial view of the business, and help us turn data into decisions.

We're hiring our first dedicated finance leader to build and own the finance function at Junction.

This is an opportunity for someone with a strong foundation in FP&A and strategic finance who wants to take on broader ownership. You'll work directly with our CEO and leaders across the company to understand what's driving the business, identify opportunities, and shape the decisions that determine our growth.

You'll also own everything that comes with building a finance function at an early-stage company, from financial planning and reporting to managing our external bookkeeping, accounting, and tax partners. You'll have the opportunity to design the systems, processes, and ways of working that will support Junction as we scale.

We're looking for someone who is as excited about building a company as they are about finance. Someone who can move between strategic analysis and hands-on execution, and who wants the breadth, responsibility, and learning that comes with being a founding finance hire.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Financial Planning & Modeling: build and own our financial model, budgets, forecasts, and scenario planning. Connect financial performance to the underlying drivers of the business and help us understand where we're going.

Strategic Business Partnership: partner with the CEO and functional leaders to evaluate growth opportunities, investment decisions, pricing, unit economics, and operational performance. Use financial analysis to help the business make better decisions.

Business Performance & Visibility: establish consistent financial reporting, KPIs, and performance analysis across the company. Bring together financial and operational data to give leadership a clear view of performance, risks, and opportunities.

Own Finance Operations: take responsibility for the company's financial operations, including accounting oversight, financial close, cash management, tax coordination, and compliance. Lead our relationships with external bookkeeping, accounting, and tax partners, ensuring the work is accurate, timely, and well managed.

Build the Finance Function: design and implement the processes, tools, reporting, and controls that Junction needs as it grows. Determine what to build internally, what to outsource, and how the function should evolve with the business.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - A trusted financial model and forecasting process that leadership uses to make decisions

 - Consistent visibility into the financial and operational performance of the business

 - Financial analysis that meaningfully informs growth, pricing, investment, and resource allocation decisions

 - A well-run finance function, with reliable reporting, accounting, tax coordination, and financial processes

 - A strong finance partnership with the CEO and functional leaders that reduces founder dependency and helps the business scale

 - A builder's mindset and an appetite for broad ownership. You're excited to take responsibility for the entire finance function, not just one part of it

title: Finance Manager
description:
Join the Rest Revolution
 The world is wired and tired. It's plagued by screens, notifications, and the sense that you should always be doing ... something. But hey, you're reading this job application right now, so you probably know exactly what we're talking about.
 So here's a bit of good news amidst all the noise: Hatch is a sleep wellness company that's betting on rest in a culture obsessed with optimization. While most technology is designed to keep you engaged, our devices use the science of habit formation to help people unplug, unwind, and recharge. Through genuinely enjoyable routines, habit building, and gentle guidance (no sleep scores or wearables here), we help people build healthier sleep habits and feel the difference in everyday life.
 More than a decade ago, we started with a mission to help parents navigate the complexities of newborn sleep. Today, we're helping more than 5 million people (and counting) take care of themselves and the people they love through the power of rest.
 We’re open to candidates across the U.S. and Canada. However, please note that Hatch is based in California, so we just ask that you're available during PST/PDT hours. 
 The Role: How You’ll Make an Impact 
 Our Finance team is looking for an FP&A Manager to join us in helping people get their best sleep yet. Reporting to the Director of FP&A, you’ll serve as a strategic finance partner and analytical engine for our business, owning revenue forecasting, demand planning, and subscription and LTV analytics, and partnering across key functions including Marketing, Retail, Operations, Analytics, and Accounting. 
 This is a high-impact role for someone who thrives at the intersection of rigorous financial modeling and cross-functional influence. You’ll be building the analytical frameworks that drive how we invest, operate, and grow—and you’ll bring a point of view to every conversation. 
 What You’ll Do 
 Revenue Forecasting & Budgeting 
- Own the driver-based revenue model end to end, from units and sell-through to registrations, subscriptions and revenue, for monthly pacing and quarterly forecasts 
- Lead the annual revenue budget and long-range plan, including scenarios that size the revenue and LTV impact of key investments 
- Run monthly actualization and forecast cycles through our FP&A platform (Datarails), keeping assumptions, scenarios and versions organized and auditable 
- Support board and investor reporting with revenue, demand and subscription metrics (units by channel, paid subscribers, ARR, attach) and a clear story on performance and outlook 
 Subscription & LTV Analytics 
- Model and track attach, conversion and retention, and maintain lifetime value and cohort contribution by product and channel, the lens Marketing uses to optimize acquisition 
- Partner with Analytics on metric definitions and data quality: pressure test the numbers, reconcile sources, and make sure the revenue model, LTV and our internal and external reporting tell the same story 
- Be the analytical bridge to Accounting on subscription deferrals and the data behind them 
 Demand Planning & Pacing 
- Lead our recurring demand outlook with Marketing, Retail and Operations, and turn the forecast into inventory, purchasing and freight decisions 
- Forecast retail sell-in and sell-through with our channel team, and track direct, retail and international pacing against plan 
- Build scenarios on product mix, promotions and supply constraints ahead of launches, promos and freight calls 
 Strategic Business Partnership 
- Bring a financial lens to growth, pricing, promotions and investment initiatives, sizing the revenue, margin and LTV impact before we commit 
- Partner with Operations on demand and supply alignment, and with our retail team on channel performance 
- Raise risks and opportunities early, with a point of view on what we should do 
 Process Improvement & Tools 
- Automate recurring pacing and reporting using SQL, Hex and Datarails, and use AI tools and agents to cut manual effort 
- Look for places where a process can be simpler, faster or more reliable, and bring them forward 
 What You’ll Bring 
- 6+ years of experience in FP&A, ideally in a consumer products, DTC and/or subscription business 
- Experience owning a driver-based revenue or demand forecast end to end, including partnering with operations or inventory planning 
- Fluency in subscription metrics (cohorts, trial and paid conversion, retention, ARR, LTV), and experience building cohort-based LTV or unit economics models 
- Advanced Excel modeling skills. SQL and a BI tool such as Hex are a strong plus; experience with an FP&A platform (Datarails, Adaptive, Pigment) or NetSuite is a plus 
- A clear communicator who leads with the "so what" and turns forecasts and variances into simple, visual takeaways for Marketing, Operations and leadership 
- Proactive and owner-minded: you raise risks early, follow through, and build structure where it doesn't exist yet 
- High attention to detail and version discipline across shared models, with the instinct to check the data before trusting it 
- BA/BS in Finance, Economics, Business, or a related quantitative field 
 Bonus points for investment banking experience or hands-on automation with SQL, Python or AI tools.  
 Why You’ll Love Working at Hatch
- We’re a certified Great Place to Work
- We help people sleep better. Our products make a real, meaningful difference in our customers’ lives
- Our team is collaborative, fun, and full of brilliant minds, and you’ll work with leadership that truly values every contribution
- We’re backed by world-class investors (and growing fast)
- We’re a remote-friendly work environment. We practice what we preach to give our employees better balance and more flexibility
 The Perks & Benefits That Matter
- 100% paid medical, dental, and vision insurance for employees (80% for dependents, including domestic partners)
- Meaningful equity. You’re an owner here
- 401(k) m

The associate will own the fund-level financial models and provide integrated planning, forecasting, performance analysis, and decision support in close partnership with the Infrastructure Equity team and finance stakeholders.
 The ideal candidate combines advanced financial modeling skills and strong accounting and financial statement knowledge with the ability to translate complex fund and portfolio data into clear insights and recommendations.
 Primary functions and essential responsibilities
 Support the FP&A VP and build effective relationships across Infrastructure Equity investment team, fund and corporate accounting, tax, divisional CFO organization, and technology teams.
 Planning, Forecasting & Performance Analysis 
- Support the annual budget, periodic forecast, and long-range planning processes for the evergreen funds within the Infrastructure Equity strategy.
- Integrate investment-level assumptions with fund-level forecasts, including investment performance, cash flows, liquidity, leverage, NAV, earnings, distributions, and investor returns.
- Analyze actual and forecasted performance, identify key business drivers and risks, and clearly explain variances against prior forecasts, budgets, underwriting cases, and realized results.

- Prepare clear, concise analyses and materials for senior leadership, investment committees, and other internal stakeholders.

- Own and maintain the fund-level financial models for the evergreen funds within the Infrastructure Equity strategy.
- Partner with investment, tax, accounting, and other stakeholders to incorporate new investments, fund developments, revised investment performance expectations, updated funding assumptions, and actual results.
- Manage the recurring fund-model input process across deal teams, including coordinating submission timelines, validating inputs, facilitating appropriate review, and escalating material changes or unresolved issues.
- Maintain model integrity through disciplined version control, documentation, reconciliation, and review procedures.
- Reconcile model outputs with investment reporting, accounting records, periodic valuations, and fund financial statements in partnership with fund and corporate accounting.
 Strategic Decision Support & Reporting 
- Translate complex model outputs into insights and recommendations supporting capital allocation, portfolio construction, financing, liquidity management, and other fund-management decisions.
- Partner with investment and tax teams to maintain accurate forecasts of taxable income, earnings and profits, and other relevant fund-level tax attributes.
- Prepare and review analyses supporting reporting packages for investors, lenders, boards, and internal committees.
- Support ad hoc financial analysis and strategic initiatives for the Infrastructure Equity team and Global Corporate FP&A leadership.
 Process Improvement, Data & Technology 
- Improve the efficiency, accuracy, and scalability of fund-level planning, forecasting, reporting, and analytical processes.
- Support the development and enhancement of dashboards, management reporting, and analytical tools.
- Identify opportunities to automate recurring workflows and leverage new technology and data solutions as they become available.
- Promote consistent FP&A practices, controls, documentation, and reporting standards.
 Qualifications

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex research, analysis, and model outputs into clear findings and presentation materials

- Expert analytical, data management, and financial modeling skills using Excel and advanced technology solutions
- Familiarity with financial planning, consolidation, reporting, and analytics applications, including Oracle, Hyperion, OneStream, Power BI, Anaplan, Alteryx, and Workiva

title: Real Estate Market Intelligence Analyst
description:
MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.




ROLE PURPOSE

Neko is opening clinics at pace: from a handful of US sites today to a 2028 cohort in the dozens and a portfolio in the hundreds by 2030. We are looking for a flexible, quantitative analyst to build the market intelligence behind that growth, using GIS, data, and analytics to decide where we open next, why, and how many clinics a market can support. The work runs from market sizing and member analytics through to site, market, and portfolio performance.

This is a build role. Neko is appointment-based, not footfall-driven, so the standard retail playbook does not transfer, and working out what predicts a successful clinic is the core problem. There is no framework to inherit: you will build the models and processes from scratch, and what you build in year one is what the whole portfolio runs on.

You will report to the Head of US Real Estate and work closely with the Transaction Managers, the Real Estate Associates, and our data analytics and engineering teams, in a small team where you help set the standard.




WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER IN THE FIRST 6-12 MONTHS

 - Market sizing: size the addressable member base by market and trade area, and translate it into how many clinics a market can support and in what order we should enter. This is the first priority of the role.

 - Site selection support: give Real Estate the analysis to justify new markets and infill locations, and to decide clinic sizing and spacing, including overlap and cannibalization as density increases.

 - Member data foundation: work with the internal data analytics and engineering teams to set up the full chain, from data collection to aggregation to analysis. Define our ideal member profile, find where those members live and work, and keep refining it as first-party data accumulates.

 - GIS platform, tool agnostic: use GrowthFactor today and own the catchment definitions, data layers, and scoring logic. Document the logic independently of the tool so it moves with us, and help evaluate and onboard the next platform when the time comes. Make the tool usable by Transaction Managers, not only by you.

 - Scoring and forecasting models: maintain a repeatable, defensible site scoring model and demand forecasts built to be re-run. A reforecast after a slipped opening or a shifted plan should be a scenario switch, not a rebuild.

 - Portfolio, market, and site performance: as clinics open, track and review performance at the portfolio, market, and site level. Compare forecast to actual, separate a bad site from a bad market from a bad launch, surface underperformers early, and document what each opening teaches us. Turn those learnings into updated site selection criteria, scoring weights, and sizing and spacing rules, so every new clinic is chosen with better information than the last.

 - Approval memos and cross-functional support: help produce LOI and Lease Approval Memos by coordinating inputs from Real Estate, Design, Construction, and Legal into a clear, one-page recommendation that leadership can decide from.

 - Process design and redesign: own the evaluation processes the team runs on, and version them. Retire what stops working, rebuild what needs it, and write it down so others can run it without you.

 - AI across the Real Estate team: use Claude and custom agents to eliminate your own manual work, then go further. Identify where AI can save broader team time (market research, data pulls, memo drafting, lease and LOI summaries, pipeline reporting), build reusable prompts, skills, and agents, train teammates to use them, and track the time saved. Be honest about where AI output needs human review.

 - Market packs and benchmarks: produce market entry recommendations, ranked pipeline views, and site-level briefs, backed by per-site cost and occupancy benchmarks by market so deal comparison sits on real data.
   
   


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3 to 6 years in real estate market analytics, site selection, location intelligence, data science, or strategy, ideally supporting multi-site physical expansion.

 - Hands-on GIS experience with GrowthFactor, Esri ArcGIS, Kalibrate, Buxton, SiteZeus, Placer, or similar. We care more that you understand catchment and scoring logic than that you know any one tool, because the tool will change.

 - Strong market sizing and quantitative skills: penetration and capture modeling, regression or other predictive approaches, and scenario and sensitivity analysis. Excel to a high standard.

 - Comfort with census, consumer spend, mobility, and first-party data, and honesty about the limits of each.

 - Financial literacy: you can build a basic site pro forma, calculate payback and break-even, and connect a demand forecast to a real estate decision.

 - Flexibility. You can tear down your own model without ego, rebuild it when the facts change, and stay organized while priorities shift.

 - Clear communication and intellectual honesty. You can defend an assumption to a skeptical executive in two minutes, name the two things most likely to be wrong, and say early when the data does not support the answer people want.

The plan converts demand forecasts and inventory policy into a rolling view of the next several weeks through the next year or more, tests that plan against labor, equipment, and material capacity, and identifies where the business cannot meet it. The Manager then drives the response to each gap, whether through training, labor, or capital investment, and hands the plan to Production Scheduling for on-site execution. The ideal candidate is a proactive people leader with a strong understanding of integrated planning systems, supply chain dynamics, and cross-functional collaboration across the operations planning team.

 - Manage finished goods inventory for compounded products within company guidance while maintaining click-to-deliver metrics for customers.

 - Develop what-if scenarios that identify where and when the plan exceeds available capacity, and which constraints are most sensitive to demand, product mix, batch size, and shift patterns.

 - Articulate and document all risks resulting from production capacity constraints, including volume at risk, timing, and effect on delivery and inventory. If the plan cannot be met, make or recommend revisions when plans cannot be met, and document the reason for each revision.

Partner with Compounding Operations, HR, and Quality to carry out approved actions and track whether each one delivers the capacity it was sized to deliver.

 - Use actual cycle times, yields, and throughput reported by Production Scheduling to update planning standards and capacity model assumptions.

title: Regional Manager of Operations, Mid-South Region
description:
Lead Regional Hospital Operations 
- Provide operational oversight and support for multiple specialty, emergency, and urgent care hospitals throughout the Mid-South region.
- Partner with hospital leadership to improve daily workflows, staffing efficiency, patient access, and overall operational performance.
- Establish consistent operational expectations while respecting each hospital's unique culture, clinical services, and business needs.
- Identify operational challenges early and work collaboratively with hospital teams to implement sustainable solutions.
- Maintain a strong field presence through regular hospital visits, leadership meetings, and ongoing communication.
 Drive Financial & Business Performance

- Partner with hospital leaders to develop and execute budgets, forecasts, and financial improvement plans.
- Monitor key performance indicators, including revenue, transactions, average transaction charges, labor costs, staffing productivity, and client experience metrics.
- Identify opportunities to improve hospital efficiency, manage expenses, and support sustainable growth.
- Translate financial data into clear, actionable priorities for hospital leadership teams.
 Develop & Empower Hospital Leaders 
- Coach and mentor Practice Managers, Hospital Administrators, and department leaders to strengthen their leadership and business management skills.
- Establish clear expectations, accountability, and consistent follow-through across hospital teams.
- Support leadership development, succession planning, and employee engagement initiatives.
- Partner with Human Resources and Talent Acquisition on recruiting, retention, performance management, and staffing strategies.
- Help hospital leaders navigate challenging conversations, organizational changes, and complex operational situations.
 Support Emergency, Specialty & Urgent Care Operations

- Partner with medical leadership to improve veterinarian scheduling, clinical support staffing, patient flow, and operational efficiency.
- Identify opportunities to improve appointment availability, service utilization, and access to veterinary care.
- Support hospital teams in managing the operational demands of extended hours, overnight services, and fluctuating caseloads.
- Collaborate with medical leaders to remove operational barriers while respecting clinical decision-making and medical autonomy.
 Strengthen Veterinary Partnerships & Client Experience 
- Build trusted relationships with Medical Directors, veterinary partners, and hospital leadership teams.
- Serve as a reliable operational resource who listens, communicates openly, and follows through on commitments.
- Partner with Marketing and hospital teams to strengthen community awareness, referring veterinarian relationships, and hospital reputation.
- Support initiatives that improve client communication, service accessibility, and the overall client experience.
- Help hospitals identify opportunities for referral growth, client retention, and stronger community relationships.
 Support Regional Growth & Strategic Initiatives 
- Partner with the Regional Vice President to execute regional priorities and operational improvement initiatives.
- Support new hospital integrations, leadership transitions, service expansions, and operational readiness as the region grows.
- Collaborate with Finance, Marketing, Human Resources, Talent Acquisition, IT, and other central support teams to ensure hospitals receive timely and effective support.
- Share best practices across hospitals and contribute to the continued development of our Specialty, Emergency & Urgent Care network.
- Help shape operational processes and leadership resources that support long-term regional growth.

- Demonstrated success improving hospital financial performance, operational efficiency, and team engagement.
- Strong financial acumen, including P&L management, budgeting, labor management, forecasting, and expense control.
- Experience coaching and developing Practice Managers, Hospital Administrators, or other hospital leaders.

- Ability to build strong relationships with veterinary professionals, medical leadership, and hospital partners.

title: Financial Institutions Senior Associate
description:
Overview: 
 The Commercial Credit Senior Associate plays a pivotal role in assessing and managing credit risk for commercial clients at M&T Bank.  This position involves analyzing financial statements, monitoring loan portfolio, and ensuring compliance with credit policies and regulatory requirements in M&T's Corporate Banking Financial Institutional Group.  This client facing role serves as a critical link between relationship managers (RM) and credit risk management to facilitate sound lending decisions and portfolio management.
 **Open to other locations within our footprint to include Boston, Baltimore, Buffalo, Rockville* *
 Primary Responsibilities: 
- Focus on transaction execution and portfolio management and partner with senior team members on complex transactions/account coverage, often under tight, syndicated finance deadlines.
- Facilitate the credit needs of customers by underwriting new requests and material modifications from deal screen through approval and for the life of the loan. This analysis may include recommending adding or removing conditions.    
- Manage the ongoing credit risk of existing loan portfolios through continuous credit monitoring activities enabling the timely identification of emerging credit risk so that appropriate actions can be taken to manage the risk, minimize losses and assign an accurate risk rating. The monitoring process includes but is not limited to annual reviews, interim update memos, a covenant monitoring program, problem loan management, early warning indicators, and other forms of credit surveillance.
- Review all pertinent credit and financial information, including but not limited to financial statements, tax returns, due diligence reports, credit bureaus, appraisals, internal credit information, industry research and peer data. Determine the need for more thorough investigation or additional information, and coordinate gathering of such information.
- Analyze financial information and related materials and complete the credit analyses for the Bank’s FIG credit transactions. Written analyses to include an independent credit quality assessment with well-supported risk rating, identification of and description of credit risks and mitigants, industry concerns, market trends, financial trends, and other pertinent credit issues of respective deals.
- Make appropriate structure recommendations based on an analysis and evaluation of scenarios including the company's case, bank's base case and a downside case.
- As part of managing the ongoing credit risk of existing portfolios, identify suspicious activity and activity that may be contrary to customer's interest.
- Partner proactively with relationship managers and be intimately involved throughout the deal process, from deal screen through approval and for the life of the loan to maintain timely and accurate risk ratings for a portfolio of commercial credits. Spread financial statements and prepare financial models designed to sensitize various conditions impacting the proposed transaction.
- Prepare cash flow, collateral schedules, covenant sensitivity calculations, financial models, and guarantor statement analysis as appropriate.
- Attend client/prospect calls with RMs to gain a thorough understanding of the client/prospect and their business to effectively analyze and underwrite the proposed transaction. Based on underwriting parameters, recommend the risk rating.
- Prepare summary, present facts, and offers opinions concerning credit-worthiness. Assist in the structure of loan requests, where appropriate, to include suggestions on terms, conditions, controls, collateral, and guarantors.
- Apply deep understanding of financial regulatory environment as it pertains to underwriting most forms of commercial credit transactions.
- Ensure credit policy compliance by verifying adherence of underwriting to the Commercial Credit Policy, and evaluating any risk associated with non-compliance Present analysis or address questions during credit request discussions or committee presentations.
- Understand and adhere to the Company’s risk and regulatory standards, policies and controls in accordance with the Company’s Risk Appetite.  Identify risk-related issues needing escalation to management.
- Promote an environment that supports belonging and reflects the M&T Bank brand.
- Maintain M&T internal control standards, including timely implementation of internal and external audit points together with any issues raised by external regulators as applicable.
- Complete other related duties as assigned.
 Scope of Responsibilities:

description:
Why Thunderbird? 
 Thunderbird is one of the world’s most trusted open-source email applications, empowering more than 20 million people globally. At Thunderbird, we build privacy-respecting communication and productivity tools that help people manage their digital lives while staying in control of their data. 
 We are open source by design. Our products are developed transparently and in collaboration with a global community of contributors, and that same spirit shapes how we work: collaboratively, inclusively, and with a shared commitment to putting users first. 
 We are a small but growing company of 70+ people distributed across seven countries. As Thunderbird evolves beyond a single desktop application, we are expanding across desktop, mobile, paid services, and new product experiences that help people and organizations work more effectively without giving up control to big tech ecosystems. 
 Our revenue model combines user donations, which help keep Thunderbird’s apps freely available, with paid services that cover the costs of hosted offerings while supporting long-term sustainability and continued innovation. 
 A note about Thunderbird and Mozilla: Thunderbird Technologies Corporation is the nonprofit-owned company behind Thunderbird email and a growing portfolio of products. While part of the Mozilla family, Thunderbird is a separate entity from Mozilla Corporation and Mozilla Foundation with its own compensation programs, benefits, and employment policies .
 To learn more, visit www.thunderbird.net 
 The opportunity 
 We are looking for a Senior Manager, Accounting & Finance to serve as Thunderbird’s most senior finance professional. The right person will bring a strong accounting or controllership foundation and the breadth to lead financial planning and analysis, finance operations, and organization-level decision support. 
 As Thunderbird grows across donations, subscription services, enterprise offerings, and international operations, our financial needs are becoming more complex. We need stronger integration across accounting and FP&A, experienced oversight of emerging revenue models and tax obligations, and clear financial analysis that helps leadership understand performance, risks, tradeoffs, and decisions. 
 Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Head of Finance will directly manage our Senior Staff Accountant and Senior FP&A Analyst. This is a hands-on functional leadership role for someone who can provide experienced financial judgment, develop an established team, and remain close to the details while helping build the systems, controls, reporting, and finance practices the organization needs for its next stage of growth. 
 This role requires regular working-hour overlap with the COO, finance team, and other colleagues across North American time zones. Candidates based in Eastern or Central time zones are preferred; candidates elsewhere in the United States should be comfortable maintaining substantial overlap with those working hours. Flexibility for meetings with colleagues, advisers, and affiliated organizations in Europe is also expected. 
 What you’ll do  
- Lead Thunderbird’s finance function, with overall responsibility for accounting, financial planning and analysis, tax, treasury, and finance operations . 
- Manage and develop Thunderbird’s finance team , establishing clear priorities, responsibilities, review practices, and accountability . 
- Oversee monthly and annual close, financial reporting, reconciliations, accounting policies, and internal controls. 
- Oversee accounting and revenue recognition across donations, subscriptions, enterprise arrangements, partnerships, and other revenue streams. 
- Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, longer-range financial planning, and scenario analysis. 
- Develop clear management reporting and visualizations that highlight important trends, risks, tradeoffs, and decisions. 
- Oversee tax, audit, indirect tax, VAT/GST, corporate filings , and related work with external advisers. 
- Evaluate the financial, tax, accounting, and operational implications of entering new jurisdictions or establishing additional entities . 
- Work with Enterprise Partnerships and Legal to establish financial reporting, reconciliation, and control processes for partner-led commercial arrangements . 
- Oversee financial reporting to Thunderbird’s parent organization and affiliated Mozilla organizations. 
- Own financial oversight of payroll across multiple providers in partnership with the People team. 
- Document and strengthen finance systems and workflows, including accounting, expense management, payment-platform reconciliation, documentation, and automation. 
- Oversee cash-flow planning, treasury, banking, and investment activities, working closely with the Senior FP&A Analyst. 
- Serve as a trusted finance adviser to organizational leaders, translating complex financial information into clear recommendations . 
 What you bring  
- 15+ years of relevant professional experience, including progressively responsible roles spanning accounting, financial planning and analysis, and finance operations. 
- Significant accounting or controllership experience, including responsibility for U.S. GAAP financial reporting, close processes, internal controls, revenue recognition, and complex accounting judgments. 
- 5+ years of people management experience in a finance or accounting environment, including coaching, feedback, prioritization, performance support, career development, and team development. 
- Demonstrated ability to improve budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, and financial data visualization and translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations for non-finance leaders. 
- Substantive experience with subscription, SaaS, digital-product, enterprise, or comparable technology-based revenue models. 
- Experience supporting partner-led commercial arrangements, such as reseller, licensing, wholesale, or reve

description:
ABOUT MERCOR



Mercor’s mission is to organize human intelligence for the AI economy. Mercor is profitable and recently raised a $750 million Series D at a $20 billion valuation. We work in person five days a week in San Francisco, New York, and London.




MERCOR AI RESEARCH FUND GRANTS: ECONOMICS OF AI

One of the biggest challenges facing the industry today is determining whether frontier AI is capable enough to deliver value in real-world settings. A model can perform well on benchmarks and still struggle in production. That’s why investing in research, realistic evaluations, and robust verification is critical.

Mercor is seeking to fund AI research on the economic impacts of AI. This is separate from the Mercor Research Fellowship, which funds individual experts (apply HERE https://www.mercor.com/careers/a0a98be0-d856-4129-b500-c0a3e412ef01/), our $5m of safety funding awards (apply HERE https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/mercor/1d59ce50-4207-4d95-b7fd-5a01e90b0897), and our funding of benchmarking research.

The grant supports:

 - The time of experts from Mercor's platform

 - Researcher hours

 - API costs

 - Stipends for event and conference attendance


BUDGET CATEGORIES

Applications are grouped into three budget tiers. Please state your tier clearly in your application and ensure your overall budget ask falls within it:

 - Tier 1: under $50,000: Suited to focused, well-scoped projects such as pilot studies, evaluations, replications, or extensions of existing work. These applications undergo a streamlined review.

 - Tier 2: under $200,000: Suited to substantial projects requiring dedicated personnel time, meaningful compute, or data collection. Reviewed with proportionally greater attention to the budget breakdown and implementation plan.

 - Tier 3: under $500,000: Reserved for ambitious, multi-component research programs. These applications receive the highest level of scrutiny: reviewers will expect a detailed justification of each spend category, a clear account of team capacity to execute at this scale, and milestones against which progress can be assessed.

The level of review scrutiny scales with the size of the ask, so applicants should request the smallest budget that credibly supports the proposed work.



 


RESEARCH AGENDA

 

We are interested in submissions in the following area:

1. Measuring AI’s impact on labor

 - How should we measure AI’s effect on real economic and labor outcomes — and what methodologies are up to the task?

 - To what extent do benchmark scores map onto real economic outcomes?

 - What is the right methodology for measuring AI’s impact on labor outcomes (employment, wages, task composition)?

 - How does occupational exposure to AI evolve over time, and how can novel datasets improve its measurement?



2. Human–AI collaboration and productivity

 - How do humans actually work with AI systems, and when does that collaboration make them more productive?

 - What is the efficiency gain of human experts when paired with AI models, and under what conditions?

 - How can we measure the “review cost” that model outputs impose on humans — the time and effort spent checking, correcting, and verifying AI work?

 - Which collaboration patterns improve output quality rather than merely output volume?



3. Enterprise adoption and returns

 - What does AI adoption look like inside organizations, and what returns does it generate?

 - How are organizations actually using AI, and how is that usage changing?

 - How can the effect of AI and agent deployments be measured causally, rather than through self-report or correlation?

 - What are the right enterprise-level variables for quantifying AI-driven productivity gains?

Applied Research at Prime

We turn a workflow into tasks, environments, evaluations, and reward signals, run post-training experiments against real baselines, and deploy what works. When a result looks good, we find out whether the gain came from the model or from the data, harness, inference, or infrastructure. The reusable parts become shared research, open-source systems, and product capabilities.

Every Applied Research role is externally facing. Most researchers work directly with customers, users, or research partners while maintaining a substantive research agenda.

Representative early problems

 - Build a quantitative-research environment where an agent forms a hypothesis, writes and runs analysis, runs a backtest on point-in-time data, diagnoses the result, and decides what to test next.

 - Design rewards and evaluations that distinguish durable improvement from the artifacts of look-ahead bias, data leakage, overfitting, favorable execution assumptions, or hidden concentration and tail risk.

ABOUT US:

Camber builds software to improve the quality and accessibility of healthcare. We streamline and replace manual work so clinicians can focus on what they do best: providing great care. ABOUT OUR CULTURE:

Our mission to change behavioral health starts with us and how we operate. We don’t want to just change behavioral health, we want to change the way startups operate. Here are a few tactical examples:

1) Improving accessibility and quality of healthcare is something we live and breathe. Everyone on Camber’s team cares deeply about helping clinicians and patients.

2) We have to have a sense of humor. Healthcare is so broken, it's depressing if you don't laugh with us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Camber is hiring an Enterprise Strategy Associate to partner with our Director of Enterprise Revenue to build the narrative behind our largest client partnerships. Revenue cycle is the bloodline of a clinic, and through data, you build trust with the client. You will drive the narrative that helps a clinic understand the impact Camber can have on its business, and you’ll use it to shape the strategy of the deal.

This is not a traditional analyst role. You will follow a clinic through its entire time at Camber, from the first conversation to a fully rolled-out partnership, and keep driving the value of Camber at every step. You will join a team that values agency, intellectual honesty, and a “rowing in the same direction” mentality.

Your time will be split across three stages of the client journey:

 - Go-to-Market: You leverage a clinic’s data to build the narrative for how Camber can impact its revenue cycle, partnering with a Director of Enterprise Revenue on the analysis and story to win the deal.

 - Implementation: You are the subject-matter expert on both Camber and the clinic, and that expertise drives how we serve them. You help make sure the value of Camber is seen and understood as we roll out.

 - Stable State: You work with the strategic account management team to inform and prepare material for the clinic’s key decision-makers to help them understand the impact Camber is having on their business.


WHAT YOU’LL DO


BE THE ANALYTICAL AND NARRATIVE BACKBONE OF THE DEAL

 - Run Diagnostics: Dig into a clinic’s billing, claims, and payment data to find where revenue is being left on the table (e.g., denial trends, underpayments, aging AR, payer-specific patterns).

 - Build the Business Case: Size the opportunity in dollars and collection rate points, and build the ROI models that decision-makers use to say yes.

 - Drive the Strategy of the Deal: Use what the data says to decide where the deal goes: which problems to lead with, what each stakeholder cares about, and what a pilot needs to prove.

 - Build Executive-Ready Materials: Turn analysis into crisp, top-down stories that client leaders can act on and take to their own leadership.


IDENTIFY WHAT REALLY MATTERS

 - Ready the Internal Team: Surface what a new enterprise account or vertical will demand (e.g., net-new integrations, custom analyses, reporting needs) and get Product, Engineering, Data, and Operations ahead of it before go-live.

 - Flag Early: Act as the account’s early-warning system. When something in the data or the relationship looks off, raise it to the right people before it becomes a fire.


ANCHOR THE CLIENT ON CAMBER’S IMPACT

 - Own the Data Relationship: Be the go-to partner for the client’s data and analytics leads through the pilot and beyond.

 - Prove and Communicate Value: Track performance against the baseline and tell the story of Camber’s impact in recurring business reviews. Delivering results is half the job. Making sure the client knows about them is the other half.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience: 1–3 years in management consulting, investment banking, or strategy at a fast-moving startup.

 - Data Fluency: Experience working with large, messy data sets and turning them into conclusions that drive decisions.

 - Customer and Executive Exposure: Previous experience working directly with customers and senior executives.

 - Commercial Instinct: You understand how businesses make money and what motivates the people making the decision, and you can tie your analysis back to both.

 - Learning Velocity: Healthcare or RCM experience is a plus but not required. What matters more is that you do your homework, ask sharp questions, and ramp quickly into a complex domain.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - The ability to turn analysis into a narrative that moves a decision, not just a data dump.

 - “Client hands”: you’re comfortable and credible in front of a client, and you can hold your ground when the room pushes back.

 - A high bar for detail. Every number you put in front of a client is one you can defend.

 - High agency: you take ownership of ambiguous problems and create structure where none exists.

 - A collaborative spirit. You know when to pull in other teams, and you aren’t shy about asking for what you need.

 - Humility: you seeak out critique and get better because of it.


PERKS & BENEFITS AT CAMBER:

 - Mental Health Support: Weekly therapy reimbursement up to $100, so you can prioritize the care that works best for you.

 - Paid Parental Leave: Up to 12 weeks of fully paid time off for new parents (birth, adoption, or foster care).

 - Financial Wellness: 401K (traditional & Roth), HSA & FSA options, and monthly commuter benefits

ABOUT THE ROLE

You have used AI tools on your own work and been frustrated by the mistakes they make. You will turn that experience into realistic Excel tasks that test how well AI does the work of a People Ops Analyst.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Writing realistic Excel tasks drawn from your own work: extending existing models, fixing broken ones and building from a brief

 - Working through each task yourself so there is a clear, correct answer

 - Writing yes-or-no criteria precise enough that a grader can mark any attempt against them
   
   


NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years in people operations, HR analytics, total rewards or workforce planning, covering headcount, compensation, benefits or org design

 - Deep hands-on Excel: headcount and comp models, named ranges, multi-criteria lookups, pivot tables and conditional formatting

 - Strong written English communication skills.

 - Attention to detail, and willingness to learn concepts in AI and Evals
   
   


ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

 - Start Date : Immediate

 - Duration: Approximately 4–6 weeks

 - Payment: task-based. Experts who complete their first task within the required timeline will then be qualified to do multiple tasks for the remainder of the project.
   
   


CONTRACT AND PAYMENT TERMS

 - You will be engaged as an independent contractor.

 - This is a fully remote role that can be completed on your own schedule.

 - Projects can be extended, shortened, or concluded early depending on needs and performance.

 - Your work at Aptura will not involve access to confidential or proprietary information from any employer, client, or institution.

 - Payments will be weekly following task completion.
   
   


GETTING STARTED

 - Apply with your details and CV. Choose an available 30-minute group walkthrough call.

 - Attend the walkthrough and create one original task from your own work. Submit the brief, the actual input workbook(s) needed to complete it. Input-file uploads are compulsory.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. The team:

We’re building the financial backbone for field service businesses. Our Fintech team is one of the most strategically important and fastest growing parts of Jobber. We help businesses get paid, access capital, understand their financial health, and ultimately stay in business longer.

The future of financial services is embedded, and we’re still early. Small businesses increasingly rely on vertical SaaS platforms like Jobber not just to run their operations, but to manage their money. Payments is the foundation of everything we do in Fintech, and how we go to market with our Get Paid products (invoicing, payments, instant payouts, etc) is the single biggest lever we have to grow the business.

You will bring together every team that touches payments go-to-market (Marketing, Sales, Account Management, Customer Support, Risk, Operations, Analytics, Product Development) and build the programs, processes, and measurement that turn these teams into a coordinated growth engine.

You'll build out Conduct's US home, from the office and the culture to the hiring and the systems behind them, while working on company-wide ops as part of a global team. It's the closest seat you can get to building a generational company, at the moment it goes global.



WHY CONDUCT

We believe the world's largest companies should move at the speed of their ideas, not the speed of the decade-old systems they run on. Today they don't.

Every process change, every new product line runs into software systems layered with decades of custom code and complexity no human mind can fully comprehend. New requirements take months to ship, system migrations cost $100M+ and years of pain.

We're building the AI operating system that absorbs this complexity and gives enterprises back their speed and ambition. Major enterprises already trust us with their most critical systems, we've closed game-changing SI partnerships, just raised a $60M Series A, and demand is outpacing what we can service.

We're a small, talent-dense team doing our life's work out of London and NYC. Extreme ownership, high velocity, low-ego collaboration. What you build here shapes the company and how the world's largest companies operate. We sponsor visas and are convinced diverse teams build better products, so we especially encourage underrepresented groups in tech to reach out.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN

You'll be the first New York-based ops hire, with a broad mandate: make sure Conduct NYC runs smoothly, both as an office in its own right and as part of one Conduct. It's a high-ownership generalist role spanning hiring, office management, finance, legal, events, and anything else you identify as needing doing.

Your first focus is completing the 0 to 1 of NYC ops. This isn't a lift-and-shift from London: you'll work out the jobs to be done in the US and deliver them, which may mean changing how we do things globally. And it's moving fast. We'll scale in NYC far quicker than we did in London, with 100+ people, a major office move, and a full events programme planned for 2027. As what you build matures, you'll hand it to new hires and trusted suppliers (likely including an office manager you'll lead). Your long-term remit will widen to global ops working closely with the Founders, whilst still retaining oversight on the NYC operation.

The motion is: build it, scale it, then manage it. The scope of the role grows as fast as the company does.

In practice:

 - Build the operational backbone of our US business, partnering with legal, finance, ops, and the Founders to put in place the systems, suppliers, and processes that let us scale fast.

 - Help us hire the next 100 people and beyond in the US: run interviews and onsites, give every candidate a great experience in our office, and help new hires land well after onboarding in London.

 - Be our first US presence in global ops. There's far more global work than we have people, and as soon as you're ramped up you'll take on real projects across the whole company, not just the US ones.

 - Run Conduct's New York office day to day, and help find, design and move into our next one.

 - Own NYC culture and events, from team rituals to partner events with the best companies in AI and tech, keeping it feeling like one Conduct with London.

 - Spot what's slowing the team down and build the fix.
   
   

WHO WE HIRE

You're sharp, organised, and ruthlessly focused on getting things done. You're hands-on from the smallest task to the largest, you love being scrappy in a fast-changing environment without clear role boundaries, and you care deeply about the people around you.

 - You're comfortable around founders, customers, and senior leaders.

 - You're highly responsible with the details that matter, from budgets to contracts.

 - You're based in New York (or ready to be) and excited to be in the office every day.

title: Business Operations Specialist
description:
About Second Front Systems

Second Front is a venture-backed company on a mission to strengthen global security by accelerating access to emerging technologies for the U.S. and our allies. Founded by Marines who saw firsthand how outdated government acquisition systems held back frontline personnel, we help commercial software companies get mission-critical technology into the hands of government users faster — backed by FedRAMP High, DoD IL2–IL6/JWICS, GovRAMP, UK MOD, and NATO authorizations. Our team is mission-obsessed, collaborative, and decisive, and we’re proud to be Great Place to Work® certified.



About the Role

Second Front Systems is looking for an organized, detail-oriented, and process-driven Business Operations Specialist to strengthen our regional operations and administrative infrastructure in the Netherlands.

This role sits at the intersection of business operations and people operations. You’ll coordinate employment, IT, and administrative workflows with the Head of EMEA and relevant global teams — translating deployment readiness and resource needs into workforce planning and operational staffing. You’ll own regional coordination, documentation, and issue follow-through across People Operations, Finance, Legal, IT, and Security, making sure deadlines, approvals, and open action items get tracked to completion.

Day to day, that means managing Dutch employment administration (contracts, right-to-work documentation, payroll inputs, leave, pension, and benefits), coordinating with payroll, HR, accounting, legal, and corporate-service providers, and maintaining regional operating records, SOPs, entity documentation, and cost-center information. You’ll act as the primary EMEA back-office point of contact across our Dutch and UK entities — the operational bridge between our regional teams, U.S. shared services, and external European providers.



Work authorization & location: Candidates must hold the right to work in the Netherlands and be based in the Netherlands (Remote).


Employment type & schedule: This position may start part-time with the opportunity to grow into full-time, and may be structured as either an employee contract or an independent services/contractor agreement — the specific arrangement, weekly hours, and schedule will be confirmed during the offer process and set out in the engagement contract. Compensation for a part-time or hourly arrangement will be pro-rated accordingly.



What You’ll Do

 - Coordinate employment, IT, legal, and administrative workflows across EMEA operations, U.S. shared services, and European providers on a regular monthly cadence.

 - Administer Dutch employment processes: contracts, right-to-work verification, payroll inputs, leave, pension, and benefits, in line with local statutory requirements.

 - Track external provider deliverables, requests, approvals, and deadlines through to completion; maintain SOPs so the work is repeatable and audit-ready.

 - Coordinate personnel-security clearance administration between EMEA, U.S. Security, NATO, and customer programs, and flag anything blocking accreditation.

 - Compile the entity and cost-center data needed for consolidated EMEA reporting, and support vendor onboarding and purchasing approval workflows.

 - Document and maintain processes that turn recurring administrative tasks into repeatable regional operations with clear ownership.

 - Translate business unit hiring needs into timelines and skill profiles aligned with mission schedules and customer accreditation gates.

 - Help resolve misalignment between finance, program management, and HR systems, and keep budget execution in sync with onboarding and deployment timelines.

 - Partner with operations leadership and People Ops on headcount allocation, role structure, and retention decisions during contract transitions.



What You Bring

 - 3–5+ years of experience in business operations, People Operations, HR operations, or cross-functional subsidiary administration.

 - Based in the Netherlands, with demonstrated experience supporting Dutch employment administration, payroll coordination, and local HR/benefits provider relationships.

 - A track record of coordinating external payroll processors, HR platforms, accounting firms, legal counsel, and corporate service providers.

 - Experience managing employment across multiple countries, legal entities, and contractor models, including employer-of-record arrangements.

 - Demonstrated discipline in maintaining organized systems for confidential employment records, legal documents, and company data.

 - Fluent written and spoken English for stakeholder coordination and documentation.



Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience supporting a U.S.-headquartered company through European subsidiaries or Dutch BV entity operations.



Compensation & Benefits

The full-time-equivalent (FTE) base salary range for this position is €65,000–€78,000 per year. If this role is engaged on a part-time or hourly basis, pay will be pro-rated from this FTE range and confirmed as part of the offer/contract. Actual compensation will depend on professional background, technical proficiency, seniority, and regional cost factors, and this role may also be eligible for equity awards and discretionary bonuses as part of a broader total rewards package.



Equal Opportunity

Second Front Systems is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, ran status, or disability status.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Corporate FP&A: Own the three-statement financial consolidation (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow), including forecasting, budgeting, and variance analysis. Sync the long-range plan with the detailed financial operating plan and monthly actuals load.

 - Monthly close: Participate in and review the monthly close, working with Accounting to make sure the numbers tie out and the story behind them is clear.

 - Equity plan forecasting: Forecast equity plan usage and dilution, and support related analysis.

 - Corporate valuation support: Support valuation work, including model inputs and analysis.

 - Team coverage: Provide backup and redundancy across the team's workstreams so that no process depends on a single person.

 - Tools and process improvement: Help implement and optimize FP&A and AI tools, and look for ways to automate and improve how the team works.

 - Executive partnership: Work directly with senior leadership and budget owners as a trusted, independent finance voice.




WHAT YOU WILL BRING

 - 8+ years of progressive finance experience, most recently with 5+ years in FP&A and 2+ years owning P&L forecasting and executive reporting at a growth-stage SaaS start-up.

 - 3-statement financial planning, including integrated P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow forecasting.

 - Deep understanding of the SaaS GTM motion, including how pipeline, bookings, and IARR/ARR connect.

 - Pricing and margin analysis, such as modeling how pricing and packaging changes affect bookings, gross margin, and unit economics.

 - Lead-to-cash process, including how billing, collections, and revenue recognition flow into ARR, deferred revenue, and cash forecasts.

 - CFA charterholder, investment banking, venture capital, private equity, or Big 4 audit experience is a plus but not required.




TECHNICAL SKILLS

 - Deep working knowledge of standard SaaS metrics (CAC payback, burn multiple, magic number, Rule of 40, net and gross retention), including how to calculate them, what drives them, and how plan assumptions move them.

 - Advanced financial modeling skills, ideally in Google Sheets as well as Excel. You design driver-based models from scratch, with assumptions you can trace and defend, rather than only updating existing ones.

 - Hands-on experience pulling and reconciling data across systems (ERP, CRM, planning tools), and a track record of using or testing AI tools to speed up finance work.




HOW YOU WORK

 - You possess a strong sense of intellectual curiosity and professional ethics.

 - Demonstrated self-initiative: you spot problems and fix them without being asked.

 - You operate independently, with a continuous improvement mindset.

 - You communicate clearly with non-finance partners and senior leaders.

 - You fit Teleport's culture and behaviors, and you do well in a fast-moving startup environment.

Some rounds, particularly those focused on your career history and past experiences, will not allow the use of AI, and we'll let you know of those in advance. When in doubt, ask your recruiter or interviewer directly.
 POSITION SUMMARY 
 Our Risk team takes a unique approach to risk management, portfolio management, and interacting with our community members. As a Staff Risk Analyst, you'll turn information into insights through analytics, data science, and experimentation to help the company achieve tremendous growth. You'll represent risk analytics for credit risk management, with a focus on limit/max policy, member retention, and forecasting.
 The base salary range for this full-time position is $173,928 – $245,773 plus equity and benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. This is a remote role in the US, however those local to Mountain View (headquarters) will require in-office work 2 days a week.

- Partner with Product to understand customer anecdotes and pain points, and design risk policy with customer experience in mind alongside risk and business outcomes

- Expert in SQL; comfortable with Python for analysis and experimentation
- Working knowledge of fintech risk fundamentals, including risk strategy development, limit/max policy, and portfolio monitoring

About Us

We also run an early-stage investment fund and an accompanying cohort program for founders. This company is not Expa, but is an affiliate of Expa's.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Research Associate who can find out anything about anything. Leadership will come to you with questions — size this market, map the players in this category, who's funding what, what the landscape looks like for XYZ — and you'll come back with an answer that's clear, well-sourced, and actually useful.

Some weeks that means building a competitive matrix across 40 companies. Some weeks it means a deep dive into a single obscure question nobody has written about yet. The projects change, the subject matter changes, and the volume varies week to week.

You'll be exposed to a lot of different projects and ideas, and work directly with a highly accomplished leader and team. If you're the kind of person who reads everything, asks a lot of questions, and wants to be in the room with people operating at a very high level, this is built for you.

What You'll Do

 - Run open-ended research projects using the internet as your primary tool: markets, products, companies, funding activity, competitive landscapes, people, technologies, regulation — whatever the question requires.

 - Turn messy findings into clean outputs: matrices, comparison tables, briefs, landscape maps, one-pagers.

 - Go deep enough to have a point of view, not just a link dump — flag what matters, what's uncertain, and what you'd look at next.

 - Use AI tools aggressively to move faster and go wider than a person could alone.

 - Build lightweight tools, scrapers, or trackers when a project calls for it.

 - Juggle several unrelated requests at once and reprioritize when things shift.

What We're Looking For

 - 2–5 years of experience and a bachelor's degree — you take a task and run with it, but you've got the reps to produce senior-level output: quick turnaround, sharp judgment calls, and less hand-holding needed along the way.

 - Brain power: sharp, curious, and able to reason through a question you've never seen before.

 - AI-native: You live in AI tools — Claude and Cowork, ChatGPT, Gemini, Hugging Face, whatever's newest. Ideally you can vibe code your way to a working script or prototype without waiting on an engineer. Bonus points if you've hit your usage limit more than once.

 - Comfortable in ambiguity: Vague briefs don't paralyze you. You take a first pass, come back with questions, and iterate.

 - Self-directed but coachable: You think independently, but you want to learn from people far ahead of you and take direction well.

 - Startup-minded: You're not looking for a corporate ladder. You want interesting problems, smart people, and range.

 - A strong writer: Your research is only as good as your ability to communicate it in a page or less.

Compensation & Benefits

 - Salary: The anticipated base salary range for this position is $100,000-$130,000. Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, level, and location.

 - Benefits: Generous benefits package including medical, dental, and vision, 401(k) matching

 - Location: Can be remote in the US, with significant travel to Los Angeles

title: Senior Health Economics and Outcomes Scientist
description:
Virta Health is on a mission to reverse metabolic disease in one billion people. Current treatment approaches aren’t working—over half of US adults have either type 2 diabetes or prediabetes, and obesity rates are at an all-time high. Virta is changing this by helping people reverse their metabolic condition through innovations in technology, personalized nutrition, and virtual care delivery reinvented from the ground up. We have raised over $350 million from top-tier investors, and partner with the largest health plans, employers, and government organizations to help their employees and members restore their health and take back their lives. Join us on our mission to reverse metabolic disease in one billion people.

As a Senior HEOR Scientist at Virta, you will play a pivotal role in proving and improving real-world health and economic outcomes for millions of patients. You will bridge cutting-edge outcomes research with commercial strategy by analyzing rich clinical and claims datasets to generate publication-grade evidence. Working cross-functionally across the data science, sales, marketing, and product teams, your work will directly shape how health plans, employers, and policy makers perceive and adopt virtual metabolic care.


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Lead the strategy, development, and execution of real-world evidence (RWE) programs and health economics models to demonstrate Virta's clinical and economic value proposition.

 - Translate complex real-world data (RWD) from health plans, employers, and external data warehouses into actionable operational and health economic insights that drive commercial growth, market adoption, and product innovation.

 - Publish findings in peer-reviewed scientific journals and present scientific evidence at national/international conferences, client presentations, and internal meetings.

 - Partner cross-functionally with sales, marketing, and product teams to integrate real-world evidence into commercial messaging, clinical care, and product development.

 - Serve as an internal subject matter expert, teaching HEOR methodologies to colleagues and advancing organizational research capabilities.


90 DAY PLAN

Within your first 90 days at Virta, we expect you will do the following:

 - First 30 Days: Onboard with the Clinical Research and Data Science teams, establish an understanding of Virta's data pipeline and existing evidence, and review current research compliance and privacy protocols.

 - First 60 Days: Take ownership of a claims dataset analysis project, collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders (Sales/Marketing) to align on evidence needs, and draft an updated HEOR strategy roadmap.

 - First 90 Days: Complete initial real-world evidence analyses, begin drafting a peer-reviewed publication or conference submission, and establish repeatable, AI-enabled workflows to streamline research and reporting tasks.


MUST-HAVES

 - Master’s degree or equivalent (PhD preferred) in Health Economics, Public Health, Pharmacoeconomics, or a related field.

 - 5+ years of experience analyzing claims/clinical datasets, publishing in peer-reviewed journals, and presenting economic outcomes of clinical programs.

 - 3+ years of business experience in a startup or high-growth environment, with proven ability to translate scientific evidence for commercial and marketplace applications.

 - Proficiency in SQL, Python, R, or SAS for conducting advanced claims analysis and data modeling.

 - Successfully designed and implemented repeatable AI-enabled workflows that address team bottlenecks and improve efficiency. For more information about AI usage in our hiring process, see Virta's AI Interview Resources page.


VALUES-DRIVEN CULTURE

Virta’s company values drive our culture, so you’ll do well if:

 - You put people first and take care of yourself, your peers, and our patients equally

 - You have a strong sense of ownership and take initiative while empowering others to do the same

 - You prioritize positive impact over busy work

 - You have no ego and understand that everyone has something to bring to the table regardless of experience

 - You appreciate transparency and promote trust and empowerment through open access of information

 - You are evidence-based and prioritize data and science over seniority or dogma

 - You take risks and rapidly iterate

Is this role not quite what you're looking for? Join our Talent Community https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/virtahealth/form/talent-community-form and follow us on Linkedin https://www.linkedin.com/company/virta-health to stay connected!

Virta has a location based compensation structure. Starting pay will be based on a number of factors and commensurate with qualifications & experience. For this role, the compensation range is $172,000-222,000/year.  Information about Virta’s benefits is on our Careers page at: https://www.virtahealth.com/careers.

As part of your duties at Virta, you may come in contact with sensitive patient information that is governed by HIPAA.
