 At Litify, we're powering a new era for the legal industry. Since its founding in 2016, Litify has helped law firms and corporate legal departments turn operations into impact through its leading AI-native Platform of Action. 
 Over 55K legal professionals and 450+ enterprise clients across plaintiff, insurance defense, immigration, and the Fortune 500 trust Litify to combine cloud-based technology, configurable AI-native workflows, agentic AI, and powerful business analytics into one open ecosystem that moves legal teams from systems of record to systems of action.
 Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and recognized as an Inc. 5000 and Deloitte Technology Fast 500 fastest-growing private company, Litify is at the center of legal innovation. Headquartered in New York, we're building the last legal platform our customers will ever need.
 About the Role
 Reporting to the CRO, we’re seeking a director-level Senior Revenue Operations Leader to solve 4 things:
- Define & Deliver a simplified, AI-forward GTM tech stack that maximizes the capture, flow, and utilization of data across the revenue process — reducing administrative burden while improving measurable outcomes.  This includes cultivating and maintaining a clean SFDC instance capable of serving as a foundation for AI initiatives.
- Elevate a business partner who operates cross-functionally: understanding, anticipating, and solving business needs through data-driven modeling and deliverables.  Serves as the trusted advisor to the CRO.
- Create company-wide consistency (when applicable) across the tech stack and reporting.
- Develop RevOps into a GTM partner for the CRO to develop, maintain, & enforce a strong operating cadence that produces definable value up and down the GTM org structure. 
 This is not a reporting-and-infrastructure seat. It is a player-coach leadership role: hands-on in the RevOps work itself, while building and leading a team that grows with the company.
 Targeted Sample Outcomes:
- A simplified, AI-forward tech stack — CRM architecture and reporting as its foundation, with AI tooling or AI builds that are actually landed and adopted by reps, proven with usage data, not a vendor selection exercise.
- Capacity and Forecast models the business trusts and can defend — bottoms-up, stage-exit criteria, conditional close rates — the data-driven modeling that makes this seat a real business partner, not just a reporting function.
- Diagnosis that turns into field-level intervention: corrective actions that reach reps with a measurable before-and-after.
 Role Responsibilities 
 Revenue Operations & Systems: 
- Own CRM architecture, hygiene, and stage-gate discipline across the full sales cycle.
- Build and maintain the bottoms-up capacity model the team's growth targets are set and defended against.
- Own revenue reporting — a single source of truth for the CRO and executive team on pipeline, bookings, and attainment.
- Run the forecast process end to end: stage-exit criteria, conditional close rates, and a cadence where managers commit their own numbers.
- Build and lead a weekly Demand Council cadence.
- Instrument competitive-presence tracking across the pipeline.
- Partner with the CRO & other members of the executive team on territory design, quota setting and modeling, and compensation plan mechanics.
 AI in the Revenue Stack: 
- Evaluate, select, and land AI tooling into the GTM stack. The bar is judgment and change management — landing something reps actually use — not necessarily building it in-house.
- Drive adoption of what gets deployed, with usage data to show it changed behavior, not just that it shipped.
- Be personally hands-on with the tools, not just directing a team that uses them — baseline Salesforce administrator fluency, plus firsthand experience connecting AI directly to the CRM (e.g., using Claude via MCP against Salesforce), not just vendor evaluation.
- Operate credibly on both sides of the point-solution question, by design: able to work within and get real value out of an existing vendor stack (Domo, Terret-style tools) and able to design and land an AI-native replacement when that's the better call. The seat is not hired to pre-commit to either philosophy — it's hired to have the judgment and the hands to execute whichever one a given problem actually needs.
 Cross-Functional Execution: 
- Drive initiatives across Sales, Marketing, and Finance without needing to own every function touched.
- Turn diagnosis into action: interventions that reach the field, with a measurable before-and-after.
 Team Leadership: 
- Build and lead the RevOps team — hiring, developing, and setting priorities as it scales with the company.
 Ideal Candidate Competencies 
- Can translate a business question into a data model — and defend that model when a sales leader disagrees with it.
- Has served as strategic advisor to a revenue leader — sat at the table for the decision, not just delivered the readout.
- Track record of putting net-new corrective actions into a field sales organization, with a before-and-after.

- Forecast discipline — can describe how they'd know the forecast was wrong before the quarter ended.
- Has selected and landed AI tooling that changed how a field team works, backed by adoption data — vendor fluency alone is a disqualifier, not a qualification.
- Has driven cross-organizational initiatives (Sales, Marketing, Finance) without owning every function involved.
- Can describe how the GTM tool stack's data actually connects, not just list the vendors in it.
- Comfortable operating hands-on at Litify's scale (~200 people) — has personally built models, not only managed analysts who did.

title: FP&A Manager

Through its advanced technology, called people magic, Mighty helps the members of those networks build relationships with each other by surfacing the most relevant and interesting connections. 
 Because of this novel approach and member-centered experience, Mighty has produced the most $1M communities and helped its Hosts earn over $500M.
 The Role
 You own FP&A at Mighty. That means the operating model, the forecast, the budget, the monthly reporting, and the analysis leadership uses to make decisions. You take a business question, find the data, build the model, and come back with an answer and a point of view, without needing someone to lay out the steps for you.
 Our SaaS community platform is the core of the business, and the launch of people magic ai will complement it. You will help leadership understand how the business is performing and where to invest.
 You report to our Head of Finance and work closely with our accounting team and with leaders across product, engineering, sales, success, and marketing. This is an individual contributor role for someone who has done this work before and wants to own it.
 What You'll Own
- You will own the company operating model and rolling forecast, covering revenue, headcount, operating expenses, and cash, and keep it current as the business changes
- You will run the annual budget and the regular reforecast process, working with department leaders to build their plans and hold them to them
- You will produce monthly budget versus actuals reporting and variance analysis, explaining what moved and why in terms leadership can act on
- You will build and maintain the SaaS metrics that describe the business, including ARR, MRR, churn, retention, customer acquisition cost, lifetime value, and gross margin
- You will model pricing, packaging, and new product scenarios and show what each one does to revenue, margin, and cash
- You will track and forecast our cost structure, including hosting, infrastructure, and third party software spend
- You will prepare the financial materials for board meetings and investor updates alongside our Head of Finance
- You will partner with accounting on the close so the numbers in the model tie to the books, and improve the systems and processes that get data from source to report
- You will take on ad hoc analysis for leadership, from hiring plans to vendor decisions to new product bets, and turn it around quickly
 What We're Looking For
- You have five or more years in FP&A, with meaningful time at a subscription software or SaaS company, and you have owned a forecast rather than contributed to one
- You can build a three-statement operating model from scratch and are fluent enough in Excel and Google Sheets that your models are clean, flexible, and easy for someone else to follow
- You know SaaS metrics well and can explain how they connect to each other and to cash
- You understand accounting well enough to work closely with a controller and staff accountants, including revenue recognition, accruals, and how the close works
- You work independently, you know what good looks like without being told, and you bring a recommendation along with the analysis
- You communicate clearly with people who are not in finance, and you can walk a department leader through their numbers in a way that changes what they do
- You are comfortable pulling data from systems such as Stripe, our general ledger, a CRM, and our product database
- You use AI tools as part of how you work, beyond prompting, whether that is building reusable skills or agents, wiring tools together to automate reporting, or knowing which parts of the workflow should stay manual
- You are accurate and careful with detail, because leadership will make real decisions on your numbers
 Bonus, none required. Any one of these moves a candidate up the list.

Vannevar builds AI systems for the Department of War's most consequential missions. We have 125 deployments across every branch and combatant command spanning our core platform and five distinct products. An an example of how we work, when major combat operations started with Iran, we fielded a new product supporting 24/7 operations and 9,000+ users in three months.
How we build is our advantage: we deploy forward with the people who own the mission. Our engineers, product team, and CTO deploy forward to the point of friction, including visiting units in Ukraine. We focus on embedding directly with operational units supporting great power competition with China, combat operations with Iran, and counter-narcotics missions.
 About the role
 We’re looking for a Senior Business Operations Manager to join a small, high-impact team that works on the company’s most important operational and strategic problems. This is a high-ownership position where you’ll drive real outcomes across the company and help us scale effectively from day one.
 In your first six months, you’ll focus on two main priorities. First, you’ll partner with leaders in our mission and engineering teams to build our system for managing customer delivery (against 9-figures of deals) and to fill gaps in the capabilities we need to execute against our customer and product priorities. Second, you’ll build the core business and operational systems and lightweight processes that will help us scale. After that, you’ll help us source, attract, and onboard the key specialized and senior talent we need for our growth areas, and work more closely within a select customer/mission area to shape the business and operating model for one of the fastest growing parts of our business.
 The role offers extensive opportunity to work with executives and leaders across the company, and growth trajectories to lead Business Operations at Vannevar or move laterally to help lead another function or line of business.
 What you’ll do
 Customer delivery and commercial operations — Vannevar has scaled to win deployments with every US Military Service and Combatant Command and with international customers, other federal agencies, and more. Each deployment carries its own delivery obligations and service objectives, and many customers have distinct practices that impact how we can operate. You’ll work with our mission and engineering teams to build a practical system to ensure seamless and efficient delivery against these obligations. You’ll partner with finance and engineering to help us understand our cost structure and opportunities for improvement, reducing friction to improve our end-users’ experience and our business performance.
 Operational systems for the business — We’ve got rapid growth plans for 2027, and need business systems and processes that enable us to scale, collect core business and financial data, and avoid taxing our employees with burdensome tasks. You’ll build and tailor tools, processes, and AI agents to solve a prioritized set of business problems, which may span finance, customer delivery, recruiting, onboarding, HR, vendor/contract management, and other business areas. You’ll build these systems such that other functions can operate them indefinitely or they can run without you, so you can solve the next set of problems.
 Strategy for senior and specialized talent — Some of the most important roles for Vannevar’s next phase of growth are ones we haven’t hired before. You’ll help prioritize roles to meet ambitious customer, mission, and product goals, and work closely with senior leadership to develop tailored plans to identify, attract, and hire the right people. You’ll then partner with recruiting to execute those plans, bringing exceptional people to Vannevar and setting them up for success.
 Business and operating model for growth areas — Once you understand the company’s priorities, you’ll go deep on a single new and high growth customer/mission area. You’ll work with the teams there to understand the growth opportunity and think creatively about the business and delivery model to unlock the next phase of growth. You’ll need to build a deep understanding of the mission problems we’re solving and how customers can leverage our tools, and combine that with business and operational judgement.
 Special projects — Some of the most interesting work you’ll do here won’t fit into a neat category. We’re a fast-growing company with a deliberately lean internal team. Important problems regularly surface and need someone sharp to own them... these problems could look like analyzing a major strategic investment, designing infrastructure for tracking a strategic goal, or identifying why a key process is breaking down and building something better.
 What we’re looking for
- ~5-10+ years of relevant work experience. You might come from a national security, management consulting, or high growth startup background — we want to see that you have experience executing and building new things. We’d love to see comfort with recruiting and building strong teams, scaling commercial and business operations, and supporting new business growth.
- Ownership and Autonomy — You care about whether things actually work, not whether you followed the right process. You take responsibility for outcomes and don’t wait to be told what to do next.
- Judgment — You figure out what the right problem is to work on, not just the one you were handed. You’re comfortable operating with ambiguity. You can decide when it makes sense to build something lightweight and fast, and when it’s worth investing more.
- Speed and Efficiency — You know how to move quickly, and to build things (processes, tools, etc.) that allow others to move quickly too. You hate time taxes or unnecessary cost and find ways to squeeze that out of systems.

title: Investor Relations Analyst
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
The Company: 
 Faraday Future (FF) is a California-based mobility company, leveraging the latest technologies and world’s best talent to realize exciting new possibilities in mobility. We’re producing user-centric, technology-first vehicles to establish new paradigms in human-vehicle interaction. We’re not just seeking to change how our cars work – we’re seeking to change the way we drive. At FF, we’re creating something new, something connected, and something with a true global impact.
 Your Role: 
 As an Analyst, Investor Relations , you'll be working with senior leadership to build stronger market-facing communication, investor engagement, and event execution capacity in New York. You'll translate company updates, executive priorities, capital markets activities, and event moments into clear, professional, and compliant communication materials. You will primarily focus on investor relations including retail investor community engagement, investor communications, roadshows, market feedback tracking, and regular IR execution support.
 This role will help strengthen the company’s communication with retail investors, monitor investor sentiment and key discussion topics, support IR materials and events, and ensure consistent, accurate, and compliant messaging across investor-facing channels.

- Support day-to-day communication and engagement with the retail investor community through approved investor relations channels, including investor inquiries, community feedback, retail investor Q&A, and investor-facing communication initiatives.

- Assist in tracking company news, market performance, peer activity, social media sentiment, shareholder feedback, and retail investor trends to support IR strategy and messaging.
- Support the preparation of management updates and internal reports summarizing retail investor sentiment, key investor questions, market feedback, and recommended communication priorities.
- Help organize and support retail investor engagement initiatives, including webinars, shareholder events, online Q&A sessions, investor community updates, and other investor communication programs.
- Assist with proofreading, formatting, and quality control of IR materials to ensure consistency across investor presentations, press releases, website updates, FAQs, and other public-facing content.

- Master or Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Communications, Marketing, Public Relations, or a related field;
- 1–2 years of experience in investor relations, capital markets, financial communications, corporate communications, equity research, finance, public relations, or related areas.
- Strong interest in public markets, retail investor behavior, shareholder communications, and listed-company investor relations.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate company updates and financial information into clear, investor-friendly messaging.
- Basic understanding of financial statements, stock market dynamics, public company disclosure, and investor communication best practices.
- Experience with social media, online communities, retail investor platforms, investor databases, CRM tools, or communication analytics is a plus.
- Strong attention to detail, good judgment, and ability to work with sensitive information in a public company environment.
- Ability to coordinate cross-functionally with Legal, Compliance, Communications, Marketing, Finance, and Capital Markets teams.
- Strong PowerPoint, Excel, Word, and general research skills.
- 1-2 years of experience in FP&A, strategic finance, treasury, corporate finance, capital markets operations, investment banking, or related finance roles.
- Strong financial modeling, forecasting, budgeting, variance analysis, and cash flow analysis skills.
- Experience working with cross-functional teams such as Finance, Accounting, Legal, Treasury, Operations, and external advisors.
- Strong Excel and PowerPoint skills; experience with SQL, Power BI, NetSuite, Tagetik, BlackLine, or other financial systems is a plus.
- Strong attention to detail, ownership mindset, and ability to manage multiple workstreams under tight deadlines.
- Ability to work in a fast-paced public company environment with changing priorities and high execution requirements.
- Strong communication skills and ability to translate complex financial information into clear management-level insights.
- Comfortable attending professional events, speaking with external contacts, coordinating follow-ups, and representing the company in a polished manner.
- Familiarity with public-company communications, investor relations, financial markets, EV, AI, Robotics, or technology industries is a strong plus.

- Translate diagnostic findings into specific vendor improvement tickets with clear success criteria — push the vendor to improve their model where the data warrants it.

 - Sharp, decision-ready written and verbal communication, including comfort presenting recommendations to senior leadership.

 - Interest in moving from an advisory seat to executing deals for a principal, in a fast-growing environment.

 - Medical, Dental, and Vision plans

 - Flexible Spending/Health Savings Accounts

OUR COMPANY

Sound like a good fit? We’d love to meet you.
